observations.title: Purchase Committee not Properly Functioning
observations.description: As per policy, Purchase Committee (PC) members should be actively involved in overseeing and execution of procurement-related functions to ensure transparency, fairness, and compliance with company policies. However, during the audit, it was observed that the committee members were not actively participating in PC-related activities.
observations.recommendation: As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/procurement/purchase-committees-pc/ - 2. Functions of PCs: “General functions of PCs would be as follows: Advise for sourcing strategy. Provide guidance for vendor management. Review and advise on whether proposed procurement actions are in accordance with this Manual. Review that equal opportunity is provided to every genuine competitor. Review and evaluate RFQ, CSQ and related documents submitted. In case of Branches, procurement process shall be handled by BPC. Review negotiated price, terms & conditions, where situation warrants. PC may choose to further negotiate with vendor for pricing, terms and conditions. Review suggestions / complaints by end users and vendors.”
observations.auditee_response: Noted.  PMC members are strictly guided to follow the procedure.

observations.title: Missing Approval for Blood Relatives & Related Family Members
observations.description: As per policy, blood relatives and related family members shall be hired with the prior approval of Head HR. It was informed, by branch, that some blood relatives / related family members were working in branch for which approval of HHR was not available. Few of the instances are as under: Sr. # Name ID Name ID Relationship 1 Ishaq Masih 17520 Bilqees Bibi 25492 Husband & Wife 2 Ambrin Javed 52150 Rehana Akash 76864 Sisters in Law 3 Shehzad Masih 82924 Razia Bibi 8932 Sister in Law of Shehzad Masih Above stated employees fall under the category as informed by branch.
observations.recommendation: As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/hrm/talent-acquisition/ - Employing Relatives: “No blood relations and related family members (including but not limiting to husband, wife, parents, children, siblings, grandparents, grandchildren and in-laws) shall be hired in the same Office/Branch; any exception shall be provided by the HHR. However, in no circumstances, one shall be allowed to be in a supervisory capacity of the other or at a position giving rise to a situation resulting in a conflict of interest. If one employee marries another, both may retain their positions provided none is in the same department or supervisory/influential capacity to the other.”
observations.auditee_response: Mentioned employees conflict of interest disclosure forms has been ready and sent to HR –ROC for approval and also noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Outgoing Attendance not Marked by Staff
observations.description: Attendance should be properly marked by all the employees. It was noted that outgoing attendance was not marked in various cases. Due to the issue, compliances of office timings cannot be verified. The matter may affect also their Leave Encashment.
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should monitor attendance record of the branch employees. Moreover, in case of attendance not marked, staff should raise application for the attendance not marked, or early leaving (whichever is applicable). As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/hrm/16-working-hours-attendance-2/2/#3--attendance - 3. Attendance: “Employees shall mark their attendance on biometric devices (online attendance) installed in offices.
observations.auditee_response: We have strictly instructed all staff to follow the guidelines.

Furthermore, positions such as Librarian, and OFA that require proper handover processes tend to experience additional delays in the settlement process.

observations.description: During the review of certain purchase transactions, it was observed that apparently the transactions were split to avoid obtaining competitive quotations, preparing a comparative statement, and issuing a Purchase Order (PO), which are required under the procurement policy for purchases exceeding the defined threshold. Few of such instances may be referred below: Soft Boards Purchase Requisition (PR) for soft board installation was made on 16-Jan-2025, with an estimated cost of Rs. 54,650. However, instead of processing the purchase through the standard procurement process, the expense was seemingly split into two transactions and processed separately on the same day. Detail may be referred below: M/s Imran Ply Wood Store: Rs. 20,100 M/s Makkah Ply Wood and Hardware Store: Rs. 21,650 The total amount of Rs. 41,750 was expended. Conservance Miscellaneous conservance related items were purchased from M/s. Super Ansari Traders in same day. Transaction of 8th Jan 2025 were amounting Rs. 19,335 and Rs. 5,720. In the same week, purchases amounting Rs. 23,770 were made from same vendor on 3rd Jan 2025. Total purchases from 1st Jul 2024 to 11th Feb 2025 were amounting Rs. 632,125. Tea Items Miscellaneous tea related items were purchased from M/s. Fargham Store in two consecutive days, and then with gap of two days. Detail is as under: Rs. 13,220 on 2nd Jan 2025 Rs. 12,640 on 3rd Jan 2025 Rs. 15,230 on 6th Jan 2025
observations.recommendation: As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/finance-audit/lfa-esl/ - 3. GENERAL: “Breaking or splitting a transaction into smaller values to avoid approval from concerned authorities will be considered a violation of this policy.”
observations.auditee_response: Noted. We will be more careful or vigilant in future.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Registration Receipts and Related Record
observations.description: During the audit certain discrepancies were found in the registration receipts and related record. Such as: Registration receipt record was incomplete. The record before, 2023 was not available. The concerned PRO was in process of matching the data with registration. Emails/Circulars for approved registration rates were not properly maintained. ID # issued in the “Registration List” was not appearing on “Registration Receipt”. This anomaly may cause a break in link of both the reports and can effect ensuring completeness of registration fee deposit. Bank deposit slips and registration receipts were not validated by branch head. Parent’s signature were found missing on certain receipts. The receipts were not properly filed in student files. As per BEAMS record, in certain instances registration fee was received from employees e.g. Name Class Receipt Number Amount Date Syeda Aroush Raza Nursery 5858810 1,300 27 January 2021 Anabia Faheem Pre-Nursery 5882382 1,300 12 October 2021 Abigail Roshan Pre-Nursery 5883540 1,300 25 October 2021
observations.recommendation: Complete record should be maintained. Relevant emails, circulars for rates, waivers, and discounts should be properly maintained for ready reference. Registration rates should be system generated. Registration ID Number may also be printed on registration receipts to create a link with registration list detail. The bank deposit slips and registration receipts should be validated by the branch head. Such control may ensure avoiding the delays, or short deposits of registration fee (if any). Parent’s signature should be obtained. As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/admission-policy/students-registration-and-admissions/2/#3--registration-process - 3. Registration Process: The PRO shall click the “Update” button to generate a Registration/System ID. The PRO shall obtain the print of the RR from the System. The RR shall be signed by the PRO and parent/guardian. Three copies of RR shall be distributed as follows: Parent’s copy (handed over to parent) Office copy (retained by Branch for record) Student file At the time of registration, “Prospectus” or “Rules Pertaining to Admission” or any other material specified by the RO shall also be handed over to the parent/student. To keep the track of admission process, Registration Receipt (RR) shall also be issued to students who are exempted from registration fee e.g. employee children, pre-mature transfers. Such receipts shall be marked as “Exempted” along with the reason/basis.”
observations.auditee_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Discrepancies in School Security
observations.description: Branch security is an important area and should be addressed accordingly. However, certain areas were identified, which were discussed with the Security Supervisor. Concerned security supervisor is requested to consider the points during planning for security and safety of the premises, after consulting RO Security Department. Few of the same are stated below: Visitor entries were not properly recorded. In certain instances, CNIC Number, Phone Number (including the numbers of vendors), Visitor Signature, Purpose of visit, etc. were missing. observations.recommendation: School management is requested to seek guidance from RO Security Department in this regard.

observations.title: Fuel Average Monitoring not Conducted
observations.description: As per policy, the Manager Admin Regional Office (RO) should ensure timely communication of the generator’s standard fuel average to the OFA. The OFA/AO is responsible for calculating and tracking the actual fuel consumption. During the audit it was observed that the Regional Office had not communicated the standard fuel average, and OFA was not monitoring the generator’s fuel consumption. This oversight can lead to untracked variances in fuel efficiency. Regular monitoring and communication are essential for better control.
observations.recommendation: As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/construction-renovation-maintenance/generator-repair-hiring/ - 2. Record Keeping (Logbook): “OFA/AO shall be informed about the standard fuel average of the genset by the relevant Manager Admin RO. OFA/AO shall calculate the fuel average of the generator on the basis of entries recorded in the logbook, after regular intervals (preferable at the time of new fueling). Fuel Average = Fuel Consumption ÷ Running Hours”
observations.auditee_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Generator Log Book not Properly Maintained
observations.description: Log book should be maintained as per company standards. During the audit, certain discrepancies were observed in this regard. Such as: Usage detail not properly updated e.g. Person making ON/OFF entry of generator was not signing. No proper record in logbooks maintained before Sep 2023. Maintenance not recorded in Logbook. Repairs/ Out of order of Generator
observations.recommendation: As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/construction-renovation-maintenance/generator-repair-hiring/#2--record-keeping-logbook - 2. Record Keeping (Logbook): “Officer Facility Administration (OFA) / Administration Officer (AO) shall maintain the record (logbook & invoices) pertinent to generator operations including fueling for their respective Branches / Offices. Following information shall be recorded in the logbook on daily basis: Date & time of diesel re-filling Quantity of fuel filled Meter readings before and after the fueling Running hours of generator and time Fuel average Replacement of parts, if any Detail of other maintenance activities e.g. change of engine oil, fuel filter, air filter etc. In case of monthly payments to third parties, invoices shall be obtained from vendor on monthly basis and be matched with the quantities recorded in the logbook. OFA/AO shall be informed about the standard fuel average of the genset by the relevant Manager Admin RO. OFA/AO shall calculate the fuel average of the generator on the basis of entries recorded in the logbook, after regular intervals (preferable at the time of new fueling). Fuel Average = Fuel Consumption ÷ Running Hours Any unusual average shall be reported to the BH / LM. Entries for fueling and running hours of generators shall be approved by the BH / LM on daily basis. Approved invoices, copies of logbook, fuel average calculation sheet and other documents, if any, shall be submitted to the BA / designated Accounts Official. BA / Accounts Official shall check the fuel average calculations, accuracy of documents submitted and record the bill in the System. The payment shall be released in accordance with the Company Policy.”
observations.auditee_response: Noted for future compliance.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Daycare Facility at School
observations.description: The daycare facility at school should be operated as prescribed in “Daycare Policy”. However, certain discrepancies were identified, few of which are; Daycare enrolment forms were not available. Although one CCTV camera was installed, but it was not able to cover the daycare completely. There were blind spots in the room. Telephone extension was not available. Warning device for fire alarm was not available. Smoke detector was not installed. Fire extinguisher was not available. First-aid kit was not available. Refrigerator was not provided. Space for Infant & Children of other ages was not separated.
observations.recommendation: As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/hrm/daycare-policy/ - Rules for Parents utilising BSS Day Care facility: “Parents must complete the daycare enrollment forms and submit them to the School Head for approval, providing the following key information: Child’s First Name Child’s Last Name Employee ID of Parent Relationship (Mother/Father) Child’s Date of Birth Emergency Phone number (1) Emergency Phone number (2)” As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/hrm/daycare-policy/ - B. Child Protection and Safety: “A CCTV must be installed in the daycare. A daycare must have a telephone extension. Emergency telephone numbers of the nearest hospital, police department, fire department, ambulance and poison control centre, along with the telephone number of the principal/headmistress should be posted near the telephone in the daycare. An early warning device shall be provided for sounding a fire alarm. An operable smoke detector must be placed in the daycare room. A fire extinguisher must also be intact in the daycare facility. A first-aid kit must be in a child care space, however, inaccessible to children. Please refer to Annexure A for Minimum requirements of a First Aid kit. A daycare centre shall have an operable, clean refrigerator.” As per https://index.beaconhouse.net/kb/manuals/hrm/daycare-policy/ - A. Operational Requirements: “Each space within a daycare facility that is used for the care of infants must be separate from spaces used by children of other ages.”

observations.title: Expenditure Exceeded the Budgeted Amount
observations.description: Budgetary limits for each expense head should be kept in view while making  expenditure. The review of system generated “Budget Variance Sheets” revealed that  significant overspending was made under different heads of accounts for the year 2021-22, 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. Detail of unfavorable variances (account head wise), is attached as Annexure-A.
observations.recommendation: The overspending should be controlled/monitored by Branch Head. Efforts should be made to spend budgeted amounts in accordance with their allocation. According to Policy: “Budget variance shall be monitored for judicious use of funds allocated under all heads of expenses. The system generated budget variance sheet should be consulted to monitor variance of expense against budget allocation and discrepancies, if any, rectified.” Imprest budget should be monitored by ROC on monthly basis. According to policy: “Monitoring of imprest budget variances of Branches shall be conducted monthly at the RO”
observations.auditee_response: Noted for future compliance. Also, there is a need to review the expenses allocated to the branch in certain heads, e.g. utilities (electricity bill). Following are the reasons for the expenditures exceeding the heads: The Building Repair and Maintenance budget increased due to the building's old age, which required significant painting and upkeep. The Consumable Equipment budget was overspent, creating a deficit, as expenses were incurred despite a lack of available funds. Computer Repair and Maintenance expenses rose due to printer refilling and repair, as well as the purchase of new peripherals (cables, mouse, and keyboards). Measures have been taken to monitor and control such expenses more effectively moving forward. However, due to the school's location and fuel price fluctuations, the expenses exceeded. Measures have been taken to monitor and control such expenses more effectively moving forward. This year, the Health and Care budget increased due to the requirements for regular dengue (pest) control and related reporting. The Utility Bill budget increased significantly due to rate hikes from the society. The Entertainment budget increased following the previous School Head's (Ms Suad Malik) directives, specifically for staff dinner and hospitality expenses. Concerns pertaining to insufficient budget should be directly raised with RO to ensure the funds are adequately issued and utilized.

observations.title: Delayed Reimbursement of Claims by RO
observations.description: Branch is being allocated limited budget against each head of account and late reimbursements to the Branch may lead to shortage of funds for smooth execution of operations. During current audit, some instances were observed where reimbursements were finalized/disbursed with significant delays to the Branch by ROC. For detail, please refer to instances below SR. NO. REF ID NARATION AMOUNT (PKR) EXPENSE DATE REIMBURSEMENT DATE DELAY IN DAYS (EXCL. 20 DAYS) 1 JV - 1 Module & Oil Filter Replacement 20 KVA Gen Set. 58,704. 01/07/2024 18/09/2024 59 2 JV - 4 Refreshment for Security guards on Annual security Training. (Paid by Humayun) 2,180 04/08/2023 20/10/2023 57 3 JV - 1 New Turbo cutter for 45 KVA generator. 45,000 01/04/2024 24/05/2024 33 4 JV - 16 8-day salary paid to substitute teacher paid by Humayun. 8,000 29/12/2023 16/02/2024 29 5 JV - 5 Expenses paid by Humayun Naseer for Annual regional Security Workshop 2024. 4,310 12/08/2024 18/09/2024 17
observations.recommendation: To avoid unnecessary delays and shortage of funds in the branch, reimbursement claims should be processed on a timely basis by ROC. As per Policy: “All reimbursement claims received shall be checked by the respective Accounts department within 20 days of their receipt”.
observations.auditee_response: Reimbursement submissions were recently delayed because the necessary approvals were secured late, even when complete bills were on file. In the future, we will ensure that advance permission is obtained for such claims within twenty days of the expenditure, guaranteeing timely presentation. Please be informed that ROC Finance handles branch reimbursement cases in a systematic manner, prioritizing them among other tasks. As a result, we cannot commit to a 20-day completion timeline, as this is not consistently achievable. Below are a few factors that cause deviations from the 20-day timeline. Some bills are based on purchase orders (POs) and are forwarded to the relevant departments (Procurement, Marketing, Construction) for PO generation, which takes additional processing time. Certain bills are received late from branches due to delays in completing the related activities and engagement in urgent tasks. Sometimes, priority items at desk is another factor of late processing the claims. Furthermore, in practical scenarios, the 20-day timeline is often insufficient for the majority of cases According to policy the bills should be cleared within the receipt of 20 days. However, any suggestions towards change in policy should be highlighted formally by the concerned department.

observations.title: Delay in Deposit of Withholding Tax
observations.description: As per company policy, Withholding Tax should be deposited within seven days from the date of deduction. However, some delays were observed in the deposit of withholding tax deducted on the payments to suppliers/vendors. Detail of instances is given in Annexure-B.
observations.recommendation: Tax policies should be strictly followed; any lapses in this regard may result in penalties to the company. As per DF letter number 10597 dated January 27, 2011: “Please follow the instructions at your end and also instruct the schools and other concerned staff to deduct the tax accordingly and Deposit the tax into Government Treasury within seven days from the deduction and payment”.
observations.auditee_response: There has been a significant reduction in these delays in the last year as compared to past performance. We will further control this in future.

observations.title: Vendors Registration Forms were not Found
observations.description: Record of all vendors, engaged in business with the branch should be filed separately and made available for verification. Whereas, it was observed that record of “Registered Vendors”, such as Vendors Registration Application (VRA) Forms and supporting documents were not available. Few instances, are mentioned below: Sr. No. Vendor 1 Ansari Brothers Network 2 Abdullah Caterers 3 We Care Pvt Ltd 4 Rehmat Ali Traders 5 Punjab Sports 6 Kings Petroleum
observations.recommendation: The concerned staff at RO/Branch should follow the procedure laid down for vendor registration. As per the Policy: “In case of procurement of goods / services at minor scale, the assessment criteria of vendors may be relaxed, however, VRF shall be filled and processed accordingly. In following cases, it is deemed that vendors are doing business with the Company at minor scale: In case of Branches – where the value of goods / services is less than PKR 25,000 per order / contract provided that the accumulated procurement from such vendor does not exceed PKR 200,000 per annum.”
observations.auditee_response: Noted for compliance.

observations.title: Quotations Avoided by Splitting the Activity
observations.description: According to Company Procurement Policy, 3 to 5 quotations are required for every transaction that exceeds PKR 25,000. During the audit, it was observed that this requirement was apparently circumvented by splitting the activity into two transactions so that quotations were no longer required to be obtained. There is a risk that the task may have been assigned at higher rates to favour vendors resulting in financial loss to the Company. Further in absence of fair competition among vendors, value for money cannot be achieved. Following are the instances: Sr. No. Date Vendor Voucher Ref Amount (Rs.) Observation 1 10.02.25 Basit Electronics JV-5 50,400 Bills splitting activity 18.02.25 Basit Electronics JV-5,16 2 10.12.24 Basit Electronics JV-4 38,550 Bills splitting activity 13.12.24 JV-10 24.12.24 JV-14 3 04.10.24 Basit Electronics JV-8 25,400 Bills splitting activity 11.10.24 JV-12 4 06.02.24 Basit Electronics JV-3 13,000 Bills splitting activity 09.02.24 JV-4 13,000 12.02.24 JV-7 13,000 5 10.01.24 Basit Electronics JV-5 24,000 Bills splitting activity 16.1.24 JV-13 16,000 Bills splitting activity
observations.recommendation: Procurement procedure should be followed as mentioned in the policies. According to Policy: “Appropriate approval is mandatory to ascertain the sanctity of any transaction. Breaking or splitting a transaction into smaller values just to avoid approval from the concerned authorities will be considered as violation of this policy.” Branch Head and concerned staff are requested to ensure the compliance with company policies at the time of approval / review of transactions.
observations.auditee_response: Noted for future compliance. All projectors will be repaired through ITO and helpdesk.

observations.title: Discrepancy in Photocopier Expenses
observations.description: Photocopy facility is available to the school staff to conduct multiple activities in school. Following are the few discrepancies noticed in Photocopier bills. Overwriting & cutting photocopies requisition slips by photocopier. The number of requested photocopies was changed on multiple instances on the same slip. Coordinator did not validate the changes made on the slips by photocopier. Accountant did not verify or cross checked the number of photocopies with the relevant teachers or coordinator and proceeded with payment.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended to prohibit the use of overwriting or cutting on the photocopy slips once signed. In case of changes, a new slip should be issued and validated by the coordinator. Accountant should ensure the compliance of the process and should not proceed with payment until verification.
observations.auditee_response: Noted for compliance. To prevent recurrence, it will be ensured that a new slip is used whenever alterations are required. Furthermore, a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has been implemented, effective from the 2025-26 academic session, to ensure due diligence at all steps before payment processing.

observations.auditee_response: Noted for compliance. Instances have reduced over the past period and we will further monitor it closely.

observations.title: Out of Order Assets Found in Branch
observations.description: All assets should be kept with due care; any damaged asset should be repaired or disposed-off. During physical verification some assets were found out of order, for which repair work was not initiated by the branch. Instances are mentioned as Annexure-F

observations.title: Document Tracking Sheet Not in Use:
observations.description: For better control over movement of documents in different offices, Document Tracking Sheet should be attached to the important documents. Contrary to this, the branch was not in practice of attaching the Document Tracking sheet with the Transfer Notes, final Settlement cases and some other documents being forwarded to different departments.
observations.recommendation: The tracking sheet should be attached to the documents being forwarded to different departments/offices. As per Policy: “DOCUMENT TRACKING SHEET” should be used on top of every such document(s) which involve movement within different organizational tiers or departments.

observations.title: High per Child Book Ratio in Library
observations.description: All libraries should have a sufficient quantity of library books. In Library of 17-G Model Town, the item per child ratio was high (as per Student Strength & Handing/Taking Report of June 2024) in the Library 48 books per student were available. The standard book ratio as decided by the Director of Studies is 15 books per child.
observations.recommendation: Keeping in view the level of students, the quantity of books should be decreased. As per Regional Librarian, the standard ratio is 15 books per student.’
observations.auditee_response: We will adjust the ratio as per above recommendation.

observations.title: Overdue Books
observations.description: Books issued should be returned within stipulated time. It was observed during the audit that some students/teachers did not return the library books. Details are mentioned in Annexure-G.
observations.recommendation: Library books should be returned back according to the company's policy. As per Policy: “Books should not be issued for more than a week”.
observations.auditee_response: Noted for Compliance, effective immediately. However, teachers are issued textbooks for the whole term because they need to use these daily. The books are returned at the end of the term. This rule should be reconsidered for the teaching staff.

observations.title: Demolition Register Not Maintained
observations.description: As per policy, a demolition register shall be maintained for scrap It was observed that no such register was not maintained at the branch.
observations.recommendation: Demolition register should be maintained by branch for scrap. As per policy: “A demolition register shall be maintained at the Branch by the Caretaker or designated person, and should be vetted by the BH and RMO.”
observations.auditee_response: Noted for compliance

observations.title: Printed Stationery Register Unvalidated
observations.description: All stock registers should be maintained properly as per company policies. During audit it was noted that printed stationary was not validated by BH.
observations.recommendation: All items should be entered in the Register and the same should be validated by Branch Head on regular intervals. As per policy: Stock Register Checked By BH Printed Stationery Designated Official Quarterly.
observations.auditee_response: The above-mentioned points have been cleared and updated and also noted for future strict compliance. During follow up visit printed stationary register was reviewed and it was noted that register was validated by BH.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Generator Log Book
observations.description: Generator Log book should be prepared, maintained as per policy and signed by the generator operator and caretaker. observations.recommendation: As per policy: “OFA/AO shall calculate the fuel average of the generator on the basis of entries recorded in the logbook, after regular intervals (preferable at the time of new fueling).” “Security Supervisor shall review the fueling process and verify the re-fueling entry by signing the logbook.”
observations.auditee_response: Noted for compliance

observations.title: Savings in Student Expenditure
observations.description: As per Company policy, savings under the category of student expenses should be avoided. During review of “Budget Variance Sheets”, it was observed that the budget for student expenditure remained un-utilized in certain heads of student expenses, for the year 2021-22, 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. The detail is attached as Annexure-H.
observations.recommendation: Budget for student expenses should be fully utilized and savings in these heads of account should be avoided. As per Policy: “There should be no saving of funds under the category of ‘student expenses”.
observations.auditee_response: Noted for compliance & more thoughtful planning and spending will be ensured in future to ensure the budget is managed effectively.

observations.title: Paid Against Extra Tax and Further Tax on Utility Bills Rs. 22,277
observations.description: During the audit, it was noted that the branch paid an additional amount of PKR 22,277 as further and extra tax on the electricity bills from every month. The branch has been incurring extra and further taxes on utility bills, which are not applicable to entities registered under the Sales Tax Act 1990 and the Income Tax Ordinance 2001. ESL is duly registered under both the Sales Tax Act 1990 and the Income Tax Ordinance 2001, making these additional taxes non-applicable. As per https://fto.gov.pk/assets/decisions/0081_om_2023.pdf, page 7: “Extra Tax: Extra Tax is being charged to industrial and commercial consumers (not registered in the active taxpayer list of FBR) @ 5% to 17%, on different bill amount slabs. Further Tax: Further Tax is being charged at the rate of 3%/4% to all consumers - having no Sales Tax Return Number (STRN) except domestic, agriculture, Bulk consumers and street light connections.”
observations.recommendation: Branch is requested to coordinate with RO, in this regard.
observations.auditee_response: Refer to RO The tax was imposed by the Model Town Society; however, the highlighted observation has already been communicated to the accountant for necessary rectification.

observations.title: Discrepancy in Cash Vouchers/Memos
observations.description: Cash vouchers/memos are made against the expenses with no proper invoice. During the audit many discrepancies were noted regarding cash vouchers that were made against several products and services. Following are the discrepancies that were noted: No supporting documents i.e. Shops/Persons visiting card, were attached with cash vouchers with details of shop or person from where the product or service was availed. There was a difference of amount noted for cash vouchers made on 13.01.2025 against an installation of doors at the branch. The vendor who worked confirmed he was paid Rs.22,000 whereas the vouchers were made of Rs.23,500 in total.
observations.recommendation: Cash vouchers should be used when invoices are not available generally for the products or services. Priority should be given to vendors who issue proper invoices. In case invoice is not issued then supporting documents which can include vendors business card or details like mobile phone number and a valid address should be attached. Subsequently cash vouchers should be made equivalently to the amount of expense actually incurred. Any intentional difference of amounts may count towards fraudulent activity.
observations.auditee_response: Payments through cash voucher will be adhered to strict compliance as suggested above. Although we believe the payment to the vendor was completed, due to the passage of time, he may have forgotten about the transaction. Cash vouchers should be signed by the person receiving the cash. In the above-mentioned case, vendor did not recognize the signatures on voucher. Henceforth cash vouchers should be signed by the vendors to confirm the receipt of cash.

observations.recommendation: Approval for blood relatives should be taken from competent authority. observations.description: Any person entering the branch is screened prior to entering the premises. During the audit it was observed that guard controlling the gate for the screening room from the inside of the branch left the gate unattended at several instances during active school hours.
observations.recommendation: Gate should only be open once the person is cleared from the security officials present in the screening room otherwise it should remain close to prevent any unauthorized entry.
observations.auditee_response: Noted for compliance During the follow up visit it was noted that the screening room was now operating as per recommendation.

observations.title: Discrepancies in School Security
observations.description: During the audit few vulnerabilities in branch security parameters were observed, which need urgent attention. Details are mentioned below; For effective lock down, all doors and windows should have grills affixed on them. During audit it was observed that doors and windows made up of glass were without any grill and were extremely dangerous in case of any unwarranted situation. Lock down being one of the most important defense tool, was not possible in these circumstances. Security supervisor room door was found open with no employee inside at multiple accounts during school hours. This room is very sensitive with regards to the stored weapons and complete access of security cameras and its vulnerability can cause issues in highly sensitive security events. During school hours walkie talkie use was often not in practice. It is important to emphasis the use of walkie talkies for effective and timely communication between security officials. It was observed that no assembly area was labelled in branch. Also, no assembly area was mentioned on Evacuation Plans present on all the floors.
observations.recommendation: It is highly recommended that branch management should look into the matter for proper resolution of highlighted issues. Moreover, Branch should put up the matter with the concerned staff at RO. Protection on glass windows and glass door of classes and offices should be fitted. As per “SOP for New Security Paradigm” chapter 3 clause 1h; “Glass windows be protected against explosions/blasts with anti-blast films/blind sheets to protect injury from flying broken glass pieces from explosions/firing.”
observations.auditee_response: Noted for compliance Grills for glass windows will be added in Capex for 2026-27 The security supervisor room will remain attended and secured at all times. The labeling of the assembly area has been completed as suggested.

observations.title: Purchase Requisition File not Maintained
observations.description: Purchase Requisition file should be maintained for ready reference. It was noted during the audit that Purchase Requisition file was not maintained by the branch.
observations.recommendation: PR file should be maintained. According policy: “There should be following copies of PR. 1st copy Retained by the Branch 2nd Copy For Invoice “
observations.auditee_response: Noted for Compliance. The Purchase Requisition (PR) file was not maintained earlier, as the copies of PRs were submitted directly to the Accountant for record. However, the school has now started maintaining a separate PR file in the library for ready reference. Going forward, will ensure that copies of all PRs are properly filed in accordance with the policy — one copy retained by the branch and the second attached with the invoice. During the follow up visit PR file was reviewed and is now maintained as per recommendation.

observations.title: Short Visits by Contractor for Walk Through Gate
observations.description: As per the generator and walkthrough gate maintenance contract, a technical person is required to visit the branch monthly for generator inspections and quarterly for walkthrough gate maintenance. However, contrary to the agreement, the contractor, M/s 4 Zee (for walkthrough gate maintenance), only conducted limited visits. The details of these short visits are provided below: Walk Through Gate Contractor Sr # Vendor Name Visit Missing Quarter Remarks 1 4 Zee Traders Sep-Nov, 2023 No Visit during this Quarter 2 4 Zee Traders Feb-Apr, 2024 No Visit during this Quarter 3 4 Zee Traders Sep-Nov, 2024 No Visit during this Quarter 4 4 Zee Traders Feb-Apr, 2025 No Visit during this Quarter
observations.recommendation: The RO should make sure that the maintenance contractor visits every branch as per mentioned in the agreements; “As AMC with M/s 4 Zee Traders “Four (04) visits for the calibration, cleaning and services of equipment will be done by the vendor “ Recovery should also be made from the contractor as per the decided rate/ratio.
observations.auditee_response: Refer to RO However, as per our contract, if a vendor fails to complete a scheduled visit, they will not be paid for it and will incur a penalty charge of fifty percent of the visit's payment. Payment is made according to the visit made. There is mentioned in the contract that If the service provider fails to visit the branch as per the agreed schedule, no payment will be made for that particular visit. In addition, a penalty/fine will also be imposed in accordance with the terms and conditions of the contract.

observations.title: Updated Maintenance Contracts not Available in Branch
observations.description: Branch should be provided with a copy of renewed annual contracts on timely basis. During the audit it was observed that annual security contract of with Zims Security Pvt. Ltd expired on June 30, 2025 but copy of renewed contracts was not provided to the branch.
observations.recommendation: To avoid uninterrupted service from contractors, and, to have clear and complete information of all the terms and conditions mentioned in annual contracts, copy of renewed maintenance contract should be available in the branch.
observations.auditee_response: Noted for Compliance Follow Up All relevant authorities are requested to inform us of the action taken with respect to the issues raised. observations.title: Expenditure Exceeded the Budgeted Amount
observations.description: Budgetary limits for each expense head should be kept in view while making expenditure. The review of system generated “Budget Variance Sheets” revealed that significant overspending was made under different heads of accounts, for the year 2019-20, 2020-21, 2021-22, 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. Detail of unfavourable variances (account head wise), is attached as Annexure-A.
observations.recommendation: The overspending should be controlled/monitored by Branch Head. Efforts should be made to spend budgeted amounts in accordance with their allocation. According to Policy: “Budget variance shall be monitored for judicious use of funds allocated under all heads of expenses. The system generated budget variance sheet should be consulted to monitor variance of expense against budget allocation and discrepancies, if any, rectified.” Imprest budget should be monitored by ROC on monthly basis. According to policy: “Monitoring of imprest budget variances of Branches shall be conducted monthly at the RO”
observations.auditee_response: Due to the impact of hyperinflation during these years, there have been some discrepancies across a few heads of accounts. However, the school has consistently made every effort to manage and maintain the budget responsibly within each category. We remain committed to adhering to established policies and ensuring that all financial practices align with the school’s operational requirements. At times, unforeseen circumstances may arise, leading to minor variations; however, we strive to address and reconcile these discrepancies promptly in accordance with policy guidelines. Moving forward, we will continue to strengthen our monitoring and planning processes to ensure greater accuracy, transparency, and financial discipline.

observations.title: Savings in Student Expenditure
observations.description: As per Company policy, savings under the category of student expenses should be avoided. During review of “Budget Variance Sheets”, it was observed that budget for student expenditure remained un-utilized in certain heads of student expenses, for the year 2019-20, 2020-21, 2021-22, 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. The detail is attached as Annexure-B.
observations.recommendation: Budget for student expenses should be fully utilized and savings in these heads of accounts should be avoided. As per policy: “There should be no saving of funds under the category of “student expenses”.
observations.auditee_response: During the academic years 2019–20, 2020–21, and 2021–22, the school operated primarily online due to COVID-19. As a result, key activities such as major school events, photocopying of student materials, purchase of sports equipment, and teaching aids were either minimized or not carried out, leading to noticeable discrepancies in those budget heads. In the year 2022–23, a portion of the budget was reserved for major school events. However, due to financial constraints and certain urgent requirements, some planned expenditures were deferred in order to prioritize and maintain the overall event plan. For the years 2023–24 and 2024–25, the allocated budget for educational visits was insufficient to meet actual costs. Consequently, school excursion trips were partially managed through cash collections. These funds were then utilized to support student activities and events, ensuring continuity of experiential learning opportunities despite budget limitations.

observations.title: Delay in Deposit of Withholding Tax
observations.description: As per company policy, Withholding Tax should be deposited within seven days from the date of deduction. However, some delays were observed in the deposit of withholding tax deducted on the payments to suppliers/vendors. The detail is attached as Annexure-C.
observations.recommendation: Tax policies should be strictly followed; any lapses in this regard may result in penalties to the company. As per DF letter number 10597 dated January 27, 2011: “Please follow the instructions at your end and also instruct the schools and other concerned staff to deduct the tax accordingly and Deposit the tax into Government Treasury within seven days from the deduction and payment”.
observations.auditee_response: We remain vigilant in ensuring that withholding tax is deposited in accordance with the prescribed policy. However, we acknowledge that there is always room for improvement, and we will exercise even greater care and diligence moving forward.

observations.title: Delayed Reimbursement of Claims by RO
observations.description: Branch is being allocated limited budget against each head of account, late reimbursements to the Branch may lead to shortage of funds for smooth execution of operations. During current audit, some instances were observed where reimbursements were finalized/disbursed with significant delays to the Branch by ROC. For detail, please refer to Annexure-D.
observations.recommendation: To avoid unnecessary delays and shortage of funds in branch, reimbursement claims should be processed on timely basis by ROC. As per Policy: “All reimbursement claims received shall be checked by respective Accounts department within 20 days of their receipt”.
observations.auditee_response: Refer to RO Please be informed that ROC Finance handles branch reimbursement cases in a systematic manner, prioritizing them among other tasks. As a result, we cannot commit to a 20-day completion timeline, as this is not consistently achievable. Below are a few factors that cause deviations from the 20-day timeline. Some bills are based on purchase orders (POs) and are forwarded to the relevant departments (Procurement, Marketing, Construction) for PO generation, which takes additional processing time. Certain bills are received late from branches due to delays in completing the related activities and engagement in urgent tasks. Sometimes, priority items at desk is another factor of late processing the claims. Furthermore, in practical scenarios, the 20-day timeline is often insufficient for the majority of cases Timelines mention in the policies & procedures should be followed by all the Departments, However, if the timelines are not practicable, those should be amended through proper procedure.

observations.title: Delay in Finalization of Final Settlement Claims
observations.description: As per company policy, final settlement claims should be processed within 45 days from the last working day of an employee. It was noted during current audit that final settlement claims of employees were being finalized with significant delay. Details are mentioned in Annexure -E.
observations.recommendation: All concerned authorities should play their role effectively for finalization of final settlement claims within the stipulated time. According to policy: “Final settlement of employees shall be paid within 45 days of their last working days”.
observations.auditee_response: Refer to RO The final settlement process through BEAMS has significantly enhanced efficiency, reducing turnaround times. However, delays in final settlements persist, particularly from July to October, primarily due to delays in profit calculations at the Corporate Finance end. Additionally, the online issuance of cheques—which takes over 2-3 weeks at the signatories end—further contributes to the delays. Instances of employees going on uninformed absences, long leaves, or not serving their notice period also result in delays, as resignation order/ end-of-employment issuances are processed based on their last working day. Furthermore, positions such as librarian, and OFA that require proper handover processes tend to experience additional delays in the settlement process. Timelines mention in the policies & procedures should be followed by all the departments. However, if the timelines are not practicable, those should be amended through proper procedure.

observations.title: All 3-Quotations were Provided by Selected Vendor
observations.description: According to Company policy, quotations should be obtained from 3 to 5 vendors for transactions exceeding PKR 25,000. During audit, certain cases were identified where this requirement was deliberately disregarded. 13 Beanbags were procured from M/S “Araish Khana” for Rs.79,950 (@ Rs.6150 each) in August 2025. It was observed, that M/S “Araish Khana” provided its own quotation along with 2 other quotations of contenders in his own handwriting. For further investigation, Audit Team visited the contenders for the verifications of their quotations, they refused to accept them as valid and declared them as fake. Purchase Committee of the Branch accepted their negligence in the collection of fake quotes. They also accepted that they were negligent in collecting the quotations from the market, they also accented that all three quotations were provided by the Vendor M/S “Araish Khana”.  Further, the PC was negligent in identifying the same handwriting of M/S “Araish Khana” on all three quotations provided. Statements of Purchase Committee Members, the other contenders are given in the Annexure-J.
observations.recommendation: Procurement procedure should be followed as mentioned in the policies. According to Policy: “Appropriate approval is mandatory to ascertain the sanctity of any transaction.” “A minimum of three vendors shall be included in the CSQ. In cases with fewer than three vendors, an exception must be granted in accordance with the 'Exception to Quotation' section." Branch Head and Purchase Committee are required to ensure the compliance with company polices at the time of approval / review of transactions. As per policy the functions of Branch PC are: General functions of PCs would be as follows: Advise for sourcing strategy. ·Provide guidance for vendor management. Review and advise on whether proposed procurement actions are in accordance with this Manual. Review that equal opportunity is provided to every genuine competitor. Review and evaluate RFQ, CSQ and related documents submitted. In case of Branches, procurement process shall be handled by BPC. Review negotiated price, terms & conditions, where situation warrants. PC may choose to further negotiate with vendor for pricing, terms and conditions. Review suggestions / complaints by end users and vendors.
observations.auditee_response: We understand the policies and procedures which are mentioned are intended to strengthen compliance with school operations. The PMC members have been  strictly advised to remain particularly vigilant in adhering to these guidelines to avoid any potential misunderstandings in the future.

observations.auditee_response: These books have been set aside as AIDN. Due to delays from the RO regarding previously approved books, these items are still being retained until the matter is resolved.

observations.title: File for Minutes of Librarian Meeting not Maintained
observations.description: File of minutes of the librarian meeting with regional librarian should be maintained by branch. During the audit it was revealed that branch was not maintaining the file for minutes of the librarian meeting.
observations.recommendation: Librarian should maintain the minutes file for reference as per library manualclause 18.1; “The Regional Librarian should call a meeting once/twice in a academic year of school librarians. All librarians are given minutes of that meeting. The librarian should file these.”
observations.auditee_response: The Librarian will maintain it from now onwards.

observations.title: File of Clearance Forms not Maintained
observations.description: File of Clearance Forms should be maintained by the branch. During the audit, it was observed that file Clearance Forms of Withdrawn Students were not prepared by the branch.
observations.recommendation: File should be prepared and updated on timely according to the Library Manual: “If a person left the system with outstanding books/library items, it should be mentioned on clearance form and keep record properly”.
observations.auditee_response: For withdrawn students, the process is documented on the Security Refund Form, which is uploaded at the time of withdrawal and signed by the School Head, PRO, and the parent. These forms are systematically filed, and access is managed by the PRO, who ensures they are properly maintained and readily available for reference. This process helps maintain transparency and accountability in the clearance and refund procedure.

observations.title: File for Reminders not Maintained
observations.description: Reminders should be issued to the person who fail to submit the issued books on time to library. A file should be kept as a record for the reminders issued. It was observed that no file for reminders was maintained in library.
observations.recommendation: Reminders should be issued for the books that are overdue and a file should be maintained for record. As per policy: “A file should be maintained with a copy of the Reminders issued to the teachers/students for not returning the books on time”
observations.auditee_response: In line with the paper-free environment promoted by Head Office, student diaries are not issued. All communication with parents is conducted digitally through Google Classroom, email, or SMS. These digital channels ensure timely, efficient, and environmentally friendly communication, while also maintaining a clear record of all interactions for reference and accountability. These modes of communications are used to keep a track with the parents.

observations.title: Discrepancies with Library Module (KOHA)
observations.description: Efficient utilization of library software (KOHA) should be ensured. Proper trainings and proper rights of the library module (KOHA) should also be provided to the librarians to ensure this. Following discrepancies were observed and subsequently confirmed by the branch librarian in discussion which seemed to be creating difficulties for the librarians in performing their day to day operations regarding library module; For branch librarian rights to view & access books were not restricted to specific branch. Auto generation of over-due books notification (email) was not in practice. Auto generation of issued & returned books notification (email) was not in practice.
observations.recommendation: Keeping in view the importance of above mentioned features which are already available in existing open source library module (KOHA), there is a need to ensure to access and practice of these options for the more controlled, efficient, accurate and scrutinized working of branch librarians by utilizing the available resources.
observations.auditee_response: Agreed with the above discrepancies

observations.title: Ex-Armed Forces Personnel not provided by Security Company
observations.description: The armed guards at the branch are provided by Parwest Pacific Security Private Limited. It was observed during scrutiny of the security guards’ that none of the 3 armed guards of the school were having ex-armed forces background, while Security Company has to provide 50% ex-armed forces personnel.
observations.recommendation: Armed guards should be provided to the branch in accordance with the contract- As per the contract, “Security Company has to provide 50% ex-armed forces personnel”. It is therefore recommended that the non-compliance of security services contract be reported to concerned office and followed up on until issues are resolved.
observations.auditee_response: It has been verbally discussed with the relevant department and we are charging the fine of Rs 100-. However, an email will also be sent to the relevant department. School security could not be compromised at the expense of penalty charges.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Maintaining Printed Stationery Register
observations.description: All stock registers should be maintained properly as per company policies. During the audit, it was observed that printed stationery register was not maintained by the branch as per policy. Following are the discrepancies observed: Closing balances of all the items were zero. Register was not validated by Branch Head
observations.recommendation: Closing balances should be calculated correctly. Register should be validated by Branch Head
observations.auditee_response: Will be maintained as guided by the Audit Team and will be signed and followed up by the SH.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Maintaining Teaching Aid Register
observations.description: All stock registers should be maintained properly as per company policies. During the audit, it was observed that Teaching Aid Register was not maintained by the branch as per policy. Following are the discrepancies observed: Closing balances of all the items were zero. Register was not validated by Branch Head
observations.recommendation: Closing balances should be calculated correctly. Register should be validated by Branch Head

observations.title: Expenditure Exceeded the Budgeted Amount
observations.description: Budgetary limits for each expense head should be kept in view while making expenditure. The review of system generated “Budget Variance Sheets” revealed that significant overspending was made under different heads of accounts. Detail of unfavourable variances (account head wise), is attached as Annexure-A.
observations.recommendation: The overspending should be controlled/monitored by Branch Head. Efforts should be made to spend budgeted amounts in accordance with their allocation. According to Policy: “Budget variance shall be monitored for judicious use of funds allocated under all heads of expenses. The system generated budget variance sheet should be consulted to monitor variance of expense against budget allocation and discrepancies, if any, rectified.” Imprest budget should be monitored by ROC on monthly basis. According to policy: “Monitoring of imprest budget variances of Branches shall be conducted monthly at the RO”
observations.auditee_response: The recommendations will be taken up for future.

observations.title: Savings in Student Expenditure
observations.description: As per Company policy, savings under the category of student expenses should be avoided. During review of “Budget Variance Sheets”, it was observed that budget for student expenditure remained un-utilized in certain heads of student expenses, for the year 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023 and 2024. The detail is attached as Annexure-B.
observations.recommendation: Budget for student expenses should be fully utilized and savings in these heads of accounts should be avoided. As per policy: “There should be no saving of funds under the category of “student expenses”.
observations.auditee_response: In 2019-20, 20-21 due to covid-19, the expenses were not incurred. Due to Government restrictions, educational visits were banned. In future we will be more careful. In 2023 -24 the remaining budget was used for other student Head of Account, i-e: Photocopy & Extra Curricular Activities.

observations.title: Delayed Reimbursement of Claims by RO
observations.description: Branch is being allocated limited budget against each head of account, late reimbursements to the Branch may lead to shortage of funds for smooth execution of operations. During current audit, some instances were observed where reimbursements were finalized/disbursed with significant delays to the Branch by ROC. For detail, please refer to Annexure-C.
observations.recommendation: To avoid unnecessary delays and shortage of funds in branch, reimbursement claims should be processed on timely basis by ROC. As per Policy: “All reimbursement claims received shall be checked by respective Accounts department within 20 days of their receipt”.
observations.auditee_response: Referred to ROC Here are few factors of late payments of reimbursement claims which need to be considered while putting this normal routine matter into the repeated observation. It should mark in a simple routine observation category. CAPEX related claims are required ERP Purchase orders (POs) to mark the budget. These claims are forwarded to the relevant departments (SC, Marketing, Admin, Security, and Works) for PO generation, which take time from initiation to final approval, sometimes more than usual, to process. Some bills are received late from branches due to delays in completing tasks. Sometimes, priority items at desk is another factor of late processing the claims. Further, in practical scenario 20 days time is insufficient for majority cases. Time lines mentioned in the Company’s policies and procedures should be followed.

observations.title: Delay in Deposit of Withholding Tax
observations.recommendation: Tax policies should be strictly followed; any lapses in this regard may result in penalties to the company. As per DF letter number 10597 dated January 27, 2011: “Please follow the instructions at your end and also instruct the schools and other concerned staff to deduct the tax accordingly and Deposit the tax into Government Treasury within seven days from the deduction and payment”.
observations.auditee_response: We have tried to deposit the Tax on time, but above-mentioned taxes are deposited with delay and we apologize in this regard. Furthermore, we will be more vigilant in the future. Recruitment, Payroll & Employees’ Record

observations.title: Delay in Finalization of Final Settlement Claims
observations.description: As per company policy, final settlement claims should be processed within 45 days from the last working day of an employee. It was noted during current audit that Final Settlement Claims of employees were being finalized with significant delay. Details are mentioned in Annexure -D.
observations.recommendation: All concerned authorities should play their role effectively for finalization of final settlement claims within the stipulated time. According to policy: “Final settlement of employees shall be paid within 45 days of their last working days”.
observations.auditee_response: Refer to RO. Compliance will be ensured of all stakeholders involved for delay.

observations.title: Livery Items Provided with Delays
observations.description: Livery items should be provided to junior staff on time. During audit we observed that livery items were provided to junior staff, with significant delays. Detail of these delays is as under; Session Due Date of Uniform Date of Delivery of Uniform Delay in Months Summer 2023 April 2023 23 June 2023 2 Winter 2023 September 2023 08 January 2024 4 Winter 2024 September 2024 06 June 2024 2
observations.recommendation: Provision of livery items to Technical and Support staff is necessary for maintaining neatness and uniformity. Livery items should be provided to the junior staff on timely basis. According to the policy: “The procurement procedure shall be initiated within time so as to provide uniform to the staff in April (Summer Uniform) and September (Winter Uniform) or in months suitable to the various Offices/ Branches, determined by RDs for their respective Regions.”
observations.auditee_response: We received some livery items with the delay from the vendor. furthermore, we will be vigilant in the future.

observations.title: Departure Attendance not marked
observations.description: Attendance should be marked while joining office at the start of day and leaving at day end. During audit, it was observed that some of the employees were not marking departure attendance on regular basis. A few of the instances are mentioned in Annexure E.
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should monitor the attendance record of the branch employees and ensure that in case of any discrepancy in attendance, staff raise their application for “Attendance Not Marked”, or “Early Leaving” (whichever is applicable) highlighting the reasons. As per policy: “Employees shall mark their attendance on biometric devices (online attendance) installed in offices.” “Employees are advised to check their attendance on the BEAMS Online Attendance Module regularly to get any errors rectified (e.g. attendance not marked).”
observations.auditee_response: Recommendations will be taken care of, in the future.

observations.title: Incomplete Student Files
observations.description: All the required documents should be filed in students’ files. Some files were selected and scrutinized during the current audit and it was found that documents like Birth Certificate, Copy of CNIC of Parents, Admission Orders and Birth certificates etc. were not available in students’ files. For details see Annexure - F.
observations.recommendation: Student files should be completed in all respects. As per Policy: “A detailed check list is attached as Annexure-2-A. This check list shall be pasted in the inner side of the file. Concerned class teacher shall ensure that all the required documents are filed in personal files of students as per the check list pasted in the file”.
observations.auditee_response: We are trying our best to complete the old Student files by giving the circulars to parents, and calling them, a copy of the circular given is also attached in file. However, the old students' school leaving cannot be placed at this time but old school reports are present in the file. While all new files being made are ensured they are complete.

observations.title: Out of Order Assets Found in Branch
observations.description: All assets should be kept with due care Any damaged asset should be repaired or disposed-off. During physical verification many assets were found for which repair work/disposal was not initiated by the branch. Detail is attached in Annexure-G.
observations.recommendation: Out of order assets should be disposed-off if they are not repairable. According to the Policy: “Assets are sold when: Assets are beyond repair or where the cost of repair is considerably high and it is considered appropriate to buy a new asset. Assets are obsolete The Company, for any other reason, has no use for the assets”.
observations.auditee_response: Above mention items will be disposed-off at earliest.

observations.title: Un-Matched Assets Found in the Branch
observations.description: Un-matched assets i.e. the fixed assets that were present in the branch but not appearing in fixed assets register were observed during the audit. Instances are mentioned in Annexure-H.
observations.recommendation: The source from which these assets were received should be identified and fixed assets’ register should be updated after consulting the matter with RO.
observations.auditee_response: The matter will be resolved after consulting with RO.

observations.title: No Action on Missing/Lost Books Reported in Stock Take
observations.description: Books should be kept with utmost care and their safe custody should be ensured. During audit it was noticed that in the Stock take report of June 2017, a number of 51 books were declared as missing but no enquiry report/fact finding details for the missing/Lost books was attached with the Stock Take Report. Detail is as follows: Year Number of Missing Books Reason 2017 51 Not Known
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that branch should check the reasons and if necessary, initiate the inquiry in coordination with ROC to find out the reasons for misplaced/lost books in this much quantity.
observations.auditee_response: This was done in previous years. Following the investigation, it was discovered that the school management did not carry out the proper handover/takeover process for the ex-librarian and did not notify the Regional Office Librarian regarding this matter. Furthermore, the current librarians at the BVTL campus did not find any missing list from the 2017 period in the library records. The Regional Office HR team has now directed the school accountant to complete the necessary process as soon as possible.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Laboratory Stock Registers
observations.description: In order to ensure smooth running of school science laboratories, laboratory stock registers and monthly consumable registers are maintained by laboratory in-charges and checked regularly by BH. Following irregularities were observed in this regard: Stock registers were not validated by Branch Head. Physical stock not matching with records. Balances were not calculated accurately.
observations.recommendation: Laboratory Stock Registers should be checked by BH on monthly basis. As per Policy: “Branch Head shall verify the laboratory registers on monthly basis.” Physical balance should be matched with the records. Closing balances should be calculated accurately.
observations.auditee_response: Recommendations will be taken care of, in the future.

observations.title: Document Tracking Sheet Not in Use
observations.description: For better control over movement of documents in different offices, Document Tracking Sheet should be attached to the important documents. Contrary to this, the branch was not in practice of attaching the Document Tracking sheet with the Transfer Notes, final Settlement cases and some other documents being forwarded to different departments.
observations.recommendation: The tracking sheet should be attached to the documents being forwarded to different departments/offices. As per Policy, “DOCUMENT TRACKING SHEET” should be used on top of every such document(s) which involve movement within different organizational tiers or departments.

observations.title: Expenses Incurred without Formal Invoices/Bills
observations.description: It was observed during the verification of Imprest Adjustments that there were many expenses incurred against which no Invoice/bill were produced. observations.title: Track Record of Quotation not Maintained by Branch
observations.description: For procurements valuing more than Rs. 100,000, a track of quotations should be filed separately and made available for verification. It was observed during the audit that track records of such procurements were not kept by the branch.
