observations.title: Electricity Sockets Bypassing the Submeter
observations.description: It was observed during the visit to Photocopiers room that 2 sockets were installed in the room of Photocopier’s which were bypassing the submeter.
observations.recommendation: All the sockets bypassing the submeter should be immediately removed from the room. Electricity consumption should be monitored for a minimum of six months. If any overutilization is observed compared to past records, the excess cost should be recovered from the vendor. Branches are not authorized to give advances/loans to other branches. Outstanding balances should be immediately settled. Cross cheque should be given to the vendors for the amount exceeding Rs. 10,000. As per policy: Payments for more than PKR 10,000 in particular and all other payments in general should be made through crossed cheques marked “Payee Account Only”. Exceptions may however be made for cheques to be issued for replenishment of petty cash/utility bills. Balance confirmation should be provided by the branch for the verification of outstanding balances. Branch should not allow him to take her assets until the clearance of due amount. Advances to employees should be settled as soon as the purpose of advance is completed. List of Preferred Vendors should be available in the branch. As per policy: “For day to day procurement activities, vendors may not be formally registered, but a list of preferred vendors shall be maintained. Officers responsible for procurement shall prepare a list of suitable vendors/contractors. This list shall be reviewed/updated by members of the Purchase Committee. The designated Officer will be responsible for maintaining and updating the list.” A list of common suppliers should be maintained by the branch in liaison with the list provided by RO. Cash in hand’s closing balance should be within the limit of Rs.25,000/-. As per Policy: “The maximum limit of closing balance of cash in hand is PKR 25,000.” The closing balance of Cash in Hand Ledger Account should not be Credit. Further, Personal Cash should not be used for the payments of Official Expenses. The branch should review its payment processes and regular reconciliation of the bank ledger should be conducted to prevent such discrepancies to ensure that the account balance accurately reflects the branch's financial standing. Cheques should not be issued to beneficiaries until the ledgers indicates availability of funds. As per Policy: “BA is responsible for recording all receipts, payments and relevant entries in the module on daily basis …….” Records for all bank signatories should be available with the branch. Bank Deposit slips should be verified by the Branch Head. Cash collection activities should be carried as per prescribed policies: All cash collection will be recorded through the ECA module. Branch Accountant shall prepare an Excel Summary of receipts & expenses for each activity and submit it to BH on a monthly basis. In case some amount is left in the balance, the same should be deposited in bank account promptly by the BA, duly reconciled with the memorandum record. Cash collection activities should be carried as per prescribed policies. Activities that are still marked as "Open" but have been completed, must be closed in BEAMS. The Branch Accountant is required to close each activity upon its completion and submit a monthly summary of receipts and expenses to the Branch Head. Probation period should not be un-necessarily prolonged and the office order for the confirmation of services should be issued on timely basis. However, in case of extension in the probation period, office order for such extension should be issued to the concerned employee. As per policy: “Unless otherwise stated in the contract of employment, all employees are required to undergo a probationary period of six (06) working months. In case of unsatisfactory performance, the Line Manager may extend probation period for an additional three (03) months.” Branch Head should monitor the working hours being served by the subordinate staff and in case of nonconformity; necessary steps should be taken for its adaptation. As per policy: “School staff shall report for duty in Branches as per the following: Staff Time In Time Out Teachers on duty 30 minutes before school starts 30 minutes after school ends Admin & Office staff 8 working hours Determined by RO All the employees’ files should be complete and updated. According to policy: “A detailed check list is attached as Annexure-3-P. This check list shall be pasted in the inner side of the file. Branch Head shall ensure that all the required documents are filed in personal files of employees as per the check list pasted in the file”. Approval for relative employees should be taken from competent authority. As per policy: “Blood relations and related family members (including husband, wife, parents, son, daughter, brother, sister, grandparent, grandchild, brother-in-law, sister-in-law, father-in-law, mother-in-law, son-in-law and daughter in-law) can only be hired in the same branch or office with the approval of the Head of HR (HHR). However, under no circumstances shall one be allowed to be in a supervisory capacity over the other, or at a position giving rise to a situation resulting in conflict of interest. Similarly, if one employee marries another, both may retain their positions provided neither is in a supervisory/influential capacity over the other. In case of concealment in any of the aforesaid situations, the Organization may take appropriate action.” Appropriate procedure should be devised and adopted at concerned levels regarding; ➢ Registration of employees. ➢ PESSI record-keeping (for instance PESSI Employee Cards). ➢ PESSI cards issued to the junior staff. Employees should also be informed about the benefits provided by PESSI for example medical care facilities and cash benefits to the secured workers and their dependents. Branch Head should ensure compliance to the company policies. The Branch accountant should keep a keen eye on these while preparations of salary. As per policy: “Off days or gazetted holidays falling in between leave periods (sandwiched) shall be counted as part of that leave. For example, if leave is applied for on a Friday and Monday, then Saturday and Sunday will be included in the leave”. Care should be taken while processing the payroll. Excessive amount should be collected from the concerned employee with the coordination of HR. Branch Head should ensure that all the receipts are deposited on timely basis. As per policy: “Cash collected as registration fee shall be deposited in the main bank account designated for collection, by close of every working week. However, in cases where the collection exceeds PKR 10,000/- the same must be deposited immediately.” Branch Head should ensure that all the receipts and deposited are correctly fed in the system. Complete information should be updated in BEAMS at an early basis. As per policy: “The PRO and Accountant shall enter Student information in Integrated Student Module (ISM) respectively at the time of admission;” Reason for the waiver in Registration fee should be mentioned in the BEAMS. Missing fixed assets should be located by the branch. As Policy: “Following authorities shall be responsible for the safe custody of the assets of the Company: Principals/Branch Heads for their respective schools”. All the Fixed Assets should be numbered as per Fixed Asset Register. As per Policy: “Upon receipt of codes, Designated Officer of User Office shall affix these codes on respective fixed assets immediately. Such codes shall be affixed in a systematic and permanent manner”. All the Fixed Assets should be numbered as per Fixed Asset Register. As per Policy: “Upon receipt of codes, Designated Officer of User Office shall affix these codes on respective fixed assets immediately. Such codes shall be affixed in a systematic and permanent manner”. All required Stocks should be entered in the Register Physical Balance should be matched with the records. Register should be validated by the Branch Head regularly. In order to keep track of annual paint work expense, branch should have an updated record of paint area measurement duly endorsed by RO. Keeping in view the level of students, the quantity of books should be increased. As per Regional Librarian, “the standard ratio is 15 books per student.” File should be prepared and updated on timely according to Policy: “If a person left the system with outstanding books/library items, it should be mentioned on clearance form and keep record properly”. Librarian should maintain the minutes file for reference as per Policy: “The Regional Librarian should call a meeting once/twice in an academic year of school librarians. All librarians are given minutes of that meeting. The librarian should file these.” Reminders should be issued for the books that are overdue and a file should be maintained for record. As per policy: “A file should be maintained with a copy of the Reminders issued to the teachers/students for not returning the books on time” Library books should be returned back according to company’s policy. As per Library Rules in Library Manual Page 21, Clause 10: “Books should not be issued for more than a week”. Keeping in view the importance of above-mentioned features which are already available in existing open source library module (KOHA), there is a need to ensure to access and practice of these options for the more controlled, efficient, accurate and scrutinized working of branch librarians by utilizing the available resources. Assembly area should be clearly labelled as per the emergency plan of branch in order to ensure smooth evacuation. At least 15 days backup time should be maintained for security purposes. As per Security Guidelines of BSS Pakistan, Clause 3D “Keep CCTV Recording/Tape for 15 days at least.” The rear gate should always be closed and should only be opened after specific caution by the security staff positioned inside the screening room. As per Chapter-4, “Charter of Duties” of Security guidelines “SOP for the New Security Paradigm” stating common duties of Chowkidar (School Guard): “Lady Searcher will knock the inner door with preset signal for Chowkidar to open and an escort from school to lead the visitor to the visited person.” Fifty percent of total guard should be retired army man, according to the contract; “Deploy well trained armed guards preferably retired from military with 50% civil/military ratio.” Generator Log book record should be updated monthly by Branch OFA and Branch Head. As per policy “Officer Facility Administration (OFA) / Administration Officer (AO) shall maintain the record (logbook & invoices) pertinent to generator operations including fuelling for their respective Branches / Offices. Following information shall be recorded in the logbook on daily basis: Date & time of diesel re-filling Quantity of fuel filled Meter readings before and after the fuelling Running hours of generator and time Fuel average Replacement of parts, if any Detail of other maintenance activities e.g. change of engine oil, fuel filter, air filter etc.” Demolition register should be maintained by branch for scrap. As per policy: “A demolition register shall be maintained at the Branch by the Caretaker or designated person, and should be vetted by the BH and RMO.” Physical Stock should be matched with the records. Register should be validated by Branch Head on regular intervals. As per policy: Stock Register Maintained BY Checked By BH Printed Stationery should be validated by Designated Official, Quarterly. Physical Stock should be matched with the records. Register should be validated by Branch Head on regular intervals. As per policy: Stock Register Maintained BY Checked By BH Sports Register should be validated by Designated Official, Quarterly.

Canteen Contractor Took Canteens Assets without Clearing the Dues It was observed during the audit that Canteen Contract ended with previous Canteen Contractor M/S Muhammad Arshad Caterer on 31.12.2024. At the time of contract end date an amount of Rs. 132,660 was due from him. Branch allowed him to remove his belongings without the payment of due amount. During audit, the vendor was called telephonically, he said that he is out of station, he will come after the Eid holidays in April 2025 to clear his dues. His assets value was not more than 20,000 and also, we do have not any store for keeping his assets. Now he said that he will come after the Eid holidays in April 2025 to clear his dues. It is bringing in your notice that when PTSL does any canteen agreement we keep a security amount just to avoid these kinds of situations. We have 57,000 with us which will be given to the campus as compensation and the remaining balance will be paid by the vendor in cash. We will be taking the follow ups. In this situation, we will also recommend blacklisting the vendor if they fail to clear their outstanding dues. The RO team should communicate and coordinate with the PTSL officials to ensure proper execution of this action. Recruitment, Payroll & Employees’ Record Delay in Confirmation of Employees Employees should be confirmed after completion of probationary period and their confirmation letters issued without any delay. In case, if the branch management needs to extend the probation period, it should be communicated to the concerned employee through probation extension letter. During audit it was observed that confirmation letter of few employees was issued with certain delays. Further, no intimation of extension of probation period was made to the concerned employees by the branch management. Following are the delays observed: ID Name Designation Category Hire Date Confirm Date Delay Months 93554 Fasiha Batool Teacher Teaching Staff 07/11/2022 01/08/2023 1 92048 Safia Tariq Housekeeping Attendant Support Staff 18/08/2022 01/04/2023 1 85979 Mubashar Abbas Teacher P.E. / Games Teaching Staff 09/08/2021 09/03/2022 1 86024 Tehreem Ishtiaq Teacher Teaching Staff 09/08/2021 09/03/2022 1 95148 Saba Pervez Teacher Teaching Staff 09/03/2023 01/01/2024 2 Refer to ROC. Confirmation extensions were processed upon recommendation of Head of School and duly shared as well. Short Office Hours Branch Head should ensure that complete office hours are being followed by the employees. During sample-based review of employee attendance, it was revealed that some of the branch staff was not following the official timings. The matter may affect operational efficiency of the Branch and also the leave encashment and salary of respective staff. Some of the instances are attached as Annexure-I. Next time we can monitor this as per the BSS Policy. Incomplete Employees’ Files Employees’ files should be completed in all respects. During checking of files during the audit it was observed that some documents like; Nomination Form, CV, Confirmation Letter & Attested Certificates etc., were missing in them as well. Instances are mentioned in Annexure-J. Next time we will be more vigilant. Related Family Employees Working in the Branch As per company policy, blood and related family members can be hired in a branch with approval of HHR. However, during random review of files we came to know of a case in which blood relatives and related family members were working in a branch against which approval of HHR was not provided/available. Moreover, branch was not maintaining any record of blood and related family members working in the same premises or otherwise. Detail of identified blood relatives is attached below; Sr. # Name Designation Relation 1 Mr. Huraira Lab Attendant Brothers 2 Mr. Hamza Assistant Accountant Above stated employees fall under the category as informed by branch personnel. Necessary action has been taken as per BSS Policy. It was verified in the subsequent audit visit that Disclosure form has been submitted by the concerned employee. Employees Record of Social Security not Available As per Punjab Govt directions, employees having salary from Rs. 17,500 to Rs 22,000 (or as prescribed by the notification issued time to time) should be registered with Punjab Employees Social Security Institution (providing hospitalization and dispensary facilities etc.) We observed that PESSI record (including copy of PESSI data form/card) of junior staff was not available and the PESSI Cards were also not issued to the Junior staff. We will start working on it. Sandwich Leaves not Considered As per BSS policies, any gazetted/official leaves that are sandwiched between the employees’ leaves will be accounted for as part of leaves and hence will be charged to the employee. During scrutiny of attendance record we found a case where sandwich leaves were not accounted for. Details are mentioned below: Employee ID Employee Name Leave Before Off Day Leave Type Off Day(s) Leave After Off Day Leave Type 86389 Nimra Asif Khan 05/08/2022 Sick Leave 06/08/2022 - 09/08/2022 10/08/2022 Long Leave She was a Transfer employee from JTC Junior Campus. She joined our campus on August 1st, 2024. Excess Salary Paid to Employee Due care should be exercised while making/transferring the salaries of employees. Any excess Payments should be reverted back/recovered from concerned staff on timely basis. It was observed during the audit that excess salary was paid to Ms. Mahnoor Rana (Teacher) for the m/o May 2022 for 7 days amounting to Rs.9,065/- Further leave Encashment was paid in double, once during regular payment of the Leave Encashment and secondly at the time of final settlement dues, amounting to Rs.2,914/- This case was wrongly done by the previous Accountant Mahnoor Rana. Leave encashment amount of Rs 2,914/- was system generated, same amount was also deducted in the Final settlement calculation. Salary reversals should be done through branch in a timely manner. Registration Fee Deposited with Delay As per Company Policy registration fee should be deposited on weekly basis or immediately where the amount of registration fee collection reaches PKR 10,000/- or more. Delays were observed while checking registration fee record. Instances are mentioned as Annexure-K. We will be more vigilant in the future. Registration Fee Deposited prior to the Collection As per Company Policy Registration fee collected should be deposited on weekly basis. It was observed during the audit that in BEAMS certain registration fee collections were deposited prior to their collection dates. Apparently, the deposit dates were wrongly fed by the concerned person. Instances are mentioned as Annexure-L. This happened mistakenly. In the future, we will be more careful. Emergency Contact Information of Students not Mentioned in BEAMS Student data should be updated at the time of feeding admission information of student. During scrutiny of student record on BEAMS in current audit, it was found that data of students i.e. emergency contact number was not entered in BEAMS. Few instances are given in Annexure-M. The emergency contact numbers are updated on Beams. Reason for Registration Fee Waiver not Mentioned Student Registration data should be complete in all respect. It was observed during the audit that the reason for Free Registration was not mentioned in the BEAMS Registration Register. Instances are mentioned as Annexure-N. This happened mistakenly. In the future, we will be more careful. Fixed Assets Remained Untraced Fixed assets represent considerable investment and therefore due care is needed for their use and safety. School Head is required to ensure the safe custody of fixed assets as per the company policy. During current audit, some of the assets appearing in the Fixed Assets Register could not be located by the concerned staff of branch. Detail of instances is as follows: Sr. No. Assets # Assets Name 1 446052 Computer CPU 2 229764 Computer CPU 3 446056 Computer CPU 4 432296 Hub Switch 5 331654 Monitor LCD Above mention, Assets are available in the Campus. Unnumbered Assets All the Fixed Assets should be numbered with the Codes assigned to them. During physical verification of assets, on sample basis, some un-numbered assets were observed in the Branch. Detail of instances are mentioned in Annexure-O. Numbers are mentioned on the Motor Bike, Water motor pump, Walkie & Talkie and Hub Switch further items are Referred to ROC and AMCO. Asset IDs have been affixed on the above assets (as mentioned by auditee). However, QR tags are placed on the Chromebooks, and these will be mapped with the asset IDs in future and displayed in the FAR. Duplicate Numbers of Assets All the Fixed Assets should be numbered with the Codes assigned to them. During physical verification of assets, on sample basis, some double-numbered assets were observed in the Branch. Detail of instances are mentioned in Annexure-P. Correct Numbers are mentioned on UPS and Bar Code Reader. And Router referred to AMCO. Discrepancies in Memorandum Record of Fixed Assets Memorandum record should be maintained by the branch as mentioned in the policies. During audit certain discrepancies were observed in the maintenance of memorandum records of fixed assets. Certain Stocks were not entered in the Register Physical Balance not matched with the records. Register was not validated by the Branch Head regularly. It's Done. Validated Paint Area Measurements not Available As paint work is a regular yearly exercise in the branch, record of paint area measurement should be available in the branch to avoid any ambiguity at the time of awarding paint work contracts. It was observed that total paintable area of branch duly endorsed by group school improvement officer was not available with branch. We will update the record. Low per Child Book Ratio in Library All libraries should have a sufficient quantity of library books. In Middle Library, the item per child ratio was low as 7.19 and 6.73 in 2023 and 2024 respectively. The standard book ratio as decided by the Director of Studies is 15 books per child. I have already informed the ROC about the low per-child book ratio and have requested an increase in the library budget to fulfil the required number of items. File of Clearance Forms not Maintained File of Clearance Forms should be maintained by the branch. During audit it was observed that file Clearance Forms of Withdrawn Students and Left Employees was not prepared by the branch. The Student Clearance forms were not submitted, which is why we were unable to maintain such files. However, we have now informed the concerned departments to follow the proper procedure, and the files will be maintained accordingly moving forward. File for Minutes of Library Coordination Meeting not Maintained Minutes of the librarian meeting with RO Librarian should be filed by branch librarian. During the audit it was observed that minutes of librarian meeting was not filed in Library files. The Minutes of Librarian Meeting file was not in practice before my joining, but moving forward, we will ensure that Minutes of Librarian Meeting file are maintained as per the required procedure. File for Reminders not Maintained Reminders should be issued to the person who fail to submit the issued books on time to library. A file should be kept as a record for the reminders issued. It was observed that no file for reminders was maintained in library. Reminders are given through Google Classroom or email by the English teacher. The file was not maintained previously because all communication and submissions were online. However, keeping the current requirements in mind, we will now create and maintain the file accordingly. Overdue Books Books issued, should be returned within stipulated time. It was observed during the audit that some students/teachers did not return the library books. Details are mentioned in Annexure-Q. The books issued to teaching staff are overdue because they require them for the entire term. On the other hand, the overdue books issued to students are those where the withdrawal was not communicated, and now we are unable to contact the students. Discrepancies in Library Module (KOHA) Efficient utilization of library software (KOHA) should be ensured. Following discrepancies were observed and subsequently confirmed by the branch librarian in discussion which seemed to be creating difficulties for the librarians in performing their day to day operations regarding library module; ❖ For branch librarian rights to view & access books were not restricted to specific branch. ❖ Auto generation of Over-due books notification (email) was not in practice. ❖ Auto generation of Issued & Returned books notification (email) was not in practice. ❖ Stocktaking through bar codes and subsequently stocktaking report generation. There is no auto-generation of Over-due & Issued & Returned books notifications. Reminders are given through Google Classroom or email Assembly area Unmarked Emergency exits and Assembly areas should be clearly marked ensuring smooth evacuation of buildings. It was observed that “assembly area” were labelled in branch. Further the allocation of designated assembly area for specific group of students were not marked such as Early Year Section, Middle Section, etc. We are working on it. Insufficient Backup time of CCTV Cameras Sufficient back up time of CCTV Cameras should be available for better security controls. It was observed during current audit that there was 10 days backup time of one DVRs having 16 CCTV cameras. Issue resolved. It was verified in the subsequent audit visit that sufficient backup facility is available for CCTV recording. In-effective Screening Room Screening room should be properly closed and locked from both sides to ensure that any visitor can only enter the building once cleared by the security staff. During audit it was noted that screening room function was in-effective as rear door was always open. Maximum times our screening room door is closed as per the Security SOP. Only at home time when our other doors are operational for student disbursement, the guards are engaged in other doors. Non Compliance of Contract for Security Guards Security Company should provide armed guard from retired soldiers according to the ratio agreed upon in the agreement. During audit it was observed that 4 guard were deputed by the Security Company and all of them were civilians. It has mentioned the security company many times. We will further communicate to the Security Company H.O for future compliance. Monetary penalties are charged to the vendor in the monthly bill against non-provision of ex-military guards. They are reminded frequently about the provision of ex-military guards as prescribed in the agreement. School security should not be compromised at the expense of penalty charges. Incomplete Generator Log Book Generator Log book should be prepared, maintained and signed by the generator operator and caretaker. During audit, it was observed that the Log Book was not maintained as per directives. Following objections were observed in this regard: No details of maintenance activities. No meter Reading mentioned. No fuel average calculated. The Generator maintenance file is separately maintained. And only Fuel averages are missing. We will complete it as soon as possible. Demolition Register Not Maintained As per policy, a demolition register shall be maintained for scrap obtained as a result of demolition. It was observed that demolition register was not maintained at branch. As per your recommendation, the New Register will be maintained. Discrepancies in Maintaining Printed Stationery Register All stock registers should be maintained properly as per company policies. During audit it was observed that Printed Stationery Register was not maintained by the branch as per policy. Following are the discrepancies observed: Physical stock was not matching with the records. Register was not validated by branch Head on regular basis Printed Stationery register were physically verified by OFA and then signed by the Principal. It was verified in the subsequent audit visit that Printed Stationery Register was maintained as per recommendations. Discrepancies in Maintaining Sports Register All stock registers should be maintained properly as per company policies. During audit it was observed that Sports Register was not maintained by the branch as per policy. Following are the discrepancies observed: Physical Stock was not matching with the records. Register was not validated by branch Head on regular basis Sports registers were physically verified by OFA and then signed by the Principal. It was verified in the subsequent audit visit that Sports Register was maintained as per recommendations. Follow Up All relevant Authorities are requested to inform us of the action taken with respect to the issues raised. observations.title: Amount Receivable from Other Branches
observations.description: It was observed during the audit that amounts were receivables from the following branches. Sr. No. Branch Amount Receivable 1 CSC Boys 2,718 2 CSC Girls 5,294 3 SA Gardens 2,718
observations.recommendation: Branches are not authorized to give advances/loans to other branches. Outstanding balances should be immediately settled.
observations.auditee_response: All balance settlement done. It was verified in the subsequent audit visit that the amounts receivables from other branches are settled.

observations.title: Payments Made in Cash Exceeding Rs.10,000
observations.description: It was observed during the audit that payments made to the vendors in cash, exceeding the prescribed limit of Rs. 10,000. Following are the instances observed. Sr. No Date Vendor Amount 1 13/02/2025 Ali Institute 90,000 2 31/10/2023 New Dynamic Engineering 36,270 3 31/10/2203 Haider Electronics 27,100
observations.recommendation: Cross cheque should be given to the vendors for the amount exceeding Rs. 10,000. As per policy: Payments for more than PKR 10,000 in particular and all other payments in general should be made through crossed cheques marked “Payee Account Only”. Exceptions may however be made for cheques to be issued for replenishment of petty cash/utility bills.
observations.auditee_response: Ali Institute demanded urgent payment that why we transferred online to his official account via advance to our OFA. Further, we will be more vigilant in the future and the rest of the Transection was directly purchased by the science teacher for a specific project.

observations.title: Balance Confirmation of Vendors were not Provided
observations.description: Following balance confirmations were not provided to audit team for the verification purposes. Sr. No Date Vendor Amount 1 19.02.2025 Muhammad Arshad Caterer 132,660 2 19.02.2025 Rainbow Interiors Zero
observations.recommendation: Balance confirmation should be provided by the branch for the verification of outstanding balances.
observations.auditee_response: We will provide as we receive from the vendors. Balance Confirmations should be provided by the branch within the period of Audit Exercise. The above balance confirmations from the vendors were not provided to audit team till the follow-up visit which was conducted on 27 May 2025, A laps of more than 3 months was observed.

observations.title: Canteen Contractor Took Canteens Assets without Clearing the Dues
observations.description: It was observed during the audit that Canteen Contract ended with previous Canteen Contractor M/S Muhammad Arshad Caterer on 31.12.2024. At the time of contract end date an amount of Rs. 132,660 was due from him. Branch allowed him to remove his belongings without the payment of due amount. During audit, the vendor was called telephonically, he said that he is out of station, he will come after the Eid holidays in April 2025 to clear his dues.
observations.recommendation: Branch should not allow him to take her assets until the clearance of due amount.
observations.auditee_response: His assets value was not more than 20,000 and also, we do have not any store for keeping his assets. Now he said that he will come after the Eid holidays in April 2025 to clear his dues. It is bringing in your notice that when PTSL does any canteen agreement we keep a security amount just to avoid these kinds of situations. We have 57,000 with us which will be given to the campus as compensation and the remaining balance will be paid by the vendor in cash. We will be taking the follow ups. In this situation, we will also recommend blacklisting the vendor if they fail to clear their outstanding dues. The RO team should communicate and coordinate with the PTSL officials to ensure proper execution of this action.

observations.title: Long Outstanding Advance
observations.description: It was observed during the audit that an advance of Rs. 78,184 was given to Mr. Waqas Ahmad for the purchase of Science Equipment on 25 November 2024 the advance was adjusted after a period of three months i-e 25 February 2025.
observations.recommendation: Advances to employees should be settled as soon as the purpose of advance is completed.
observations.auditee_response: We have already adjusted the advance amount in Feb Imprest as we received the bills. That advance was issued against a specific purpose for senior students' science projects. A period of 3 months was observed to settle the advance amount.

observations.title: List of Preferred Vendors not Available in the Branch
observations.description: List of Preferred Vendors should be available in the branch. During audit it was observed that the said lists were not available in the branch.
observations.recommendation: List of Preferred Vendors should be available in the branch. As per policy: “For day to day procurement activities, vendors may not be formally registered, but a list of preferred vendors shall be maintained. Officers responsible for procurement shall prepare a list of suitable vendors/contractors. This list shall be reviewed/updated by members of the Purchase Committee. The designated Officer will be responsible for maintaining and updating the list.”
observations.auditee_response: List of preferred vendors was not available, further, we will maintain in future.

observations.title: List of Common Supplier Not provided by RO
observations.description: RO should maintain and circulate a list of suppliers that are commonly used by the branches and RO. During Audit, it was observed that RO did not share the common suppliers lists with the branches.
observations.recommendation: A list of common suppliers should be maintained by the branch in liaison with the list provided by RO.
observations.auditee_response: The list of Common Vendors not received from ROC. The Common Vendor list has already been given to the branches. Latest List of Common suppliers should also be shared with the branches.

observations.title: Cash in Hand Exceeding Prescribed Limit
observations.recommendation: Cash in hand’s closing balance should be within the limit of Rs.25,000/-. As per Policy: “The maximum limit of closing balance of cash in hand is PKR 25,000.”
observations.auditee_response: This happened mistakenly. In the future we will be more careful.

observations.title: Credit Balance of Cash In Hand
observations.description: Balance of Cash in Hand Ledger Account should not be negative. During audit it was observed that closing balance of the ledger account was credit at multiple occasions. Instances are mentioned in below table: Sr. No. DATE BALANCE Debit/ Cr. 1 06/02/2020 624 Cr. 2 03/06/2021 387 Cr. 3 12/08/2021 383 Cr. 4 21/02/2022 1,095 Cr. 5 02/03/2022 4,169 Cr. 6 07/03/2022 5,820 Cr. 7 21/03/2022 3,718 Cr. 8 22/03/2022 4,638 Cr. 9 24/02/2025 5,388 Cr.
observations.recommendation: The closing balance of Cash in Hand Ledger Account should not be Credit. Further, Personal Cash should not be used for the payments of Official Expenses.
observations.auditee_response: This happened mistakenly. In the future we will be more careful.

observations.title: Credit Balance of Bank Ledger Account
observations.description: Bank Account usually show a balance in debit indicating available funds. During audit it was observed that bank ledger went into a credit of balance when payments were made indicating negative balance at bank which is not a true presentation of accounts. Instances are mentioned in below table: It was observed that the balance of bank ledger maintained by the branch, was negative at end of day (on certain occasions). This negative balance indicates a mismatch between the recorded transactions and the actual available funds in the account. Few of the instances may be referred as follows: Sr. No. DATE BALANCE Debit/ Cr 1 30/09/2020 131,686.74 Cr 2 05/10/2020 130,784.00 Cr 3 09/04/2021 4,389.34 Cr 4 13/04/2021 4,621.34 Cr
observations.recommendation: The branch should review its payment processes and regular reconciliation of the bank ledger should be conducted to prevent such discrepancies to ensure that the account balance accurately reflects the branch's financial standing. Cheques should not be issued to beneficiaries until the ledgers indicates availability of funds. As per Policy: “BA is responsible for recording all receipts, payments and relevant entries in the module on daily basis …….”
observations.auditee_response: This happened mistakenly. In the future we will be more careful.

observations.title: Record for Bank Signatories not Available in Branch
observations.description: Records for all bank signatories should be available with the branch. It was observed during the audit that the records available in the branch with respect to Bank Signatories were for two signatories only i-e Branch Head and Branch Accountant. Rest of Signatories from ROC and HO were not communicated to the Branch.
observations.recommendation: Records for all bank signatories should be available with the branch.
observations.auditee_response: The updated signatories document was not received from ROC. Updated signatories list now provided to the branch. It was verified in the subsequent audit visit that the updated signatories document was received from ROC.

observations.title: Cash Collection Activities not being Properly Maintained
observations.description: It was observed during the verification of Cash Collection Activities in BEAMS records that a cash collection of Rs. 1,166,520 was made in October 2024 for Melange Activity. Following Discrepancies were observed in the activity: Activity was not entered in BEAMS. Bills were not approved.. Record for the collection activities amounting to Rs. 313,700 could not be produced by the Branch Accountant, Detail an s below: Sr. No Cash collected from: Amount 1 Social Passes (Qawali Night & Concert) 186,500 2 Cash Registrations 127,200 TOTAL 313,700 Balance of Rs. 83,727 was not deposited in the bank. C.S.Qs and Quotations were not taken for the expenses exceeding Rs.25,000.
observations.recommendation: Cash collection activities should be carried as per prescribed policies: All cash collection will be recorded through the ECA module. Branch Accountant shall prepare an Excel Summary of receipts & expenses for each activity and submit it to BH on a monthly basis. In case some amount is left in the balance, the same should be deposited in bank account promptly by the BA, duly reconciled with the memorandum record. Cash collection activities should be carried as per prescribed policies.
observations.auditee_response: Next time we will take care of it. Instructed to the lead Accountant for strict future compliance. observations.title: Cash Collection and Expenditure for Melange Activity was not properly maintained
observations.description: It was observed during the sample verification of Cash Collection Activities in BEAMS records that a cash collection of Rs. 473,500 was made in November 2022. Following Discrepancies were observed in the activity: Activity was not entered in BEAMS. No record for the collection of amounts were kept for verifications. No bill was approved by Branch Head. CSQ and quotation were not taken for the expenses exceeding Rs.25,000.
observations.recommendation: Cash collection activities should be carried as per prescribed policies. Activities that are still marked as "Open" but have been completed, must be closed in BEAMS. The Branch Accountant is required to close each activity upon its completion and submit a monthly summary of receipts and expenses to the Branch Head. Probation period should not be un-necessarily prolonged and the office order for the confirmation of services should be issued on timely basis. However, in case of extension in the probation period, office order for such extension should be issued to the concerned employee. As per policy: “Unless otherwise stated in the contract of employment, all employees are required to undergo a probationary period of six (06) working months. In case of unsatisfactory performance, the Line Manager may extend probation period for an additional three (03) months.” Branch Head should monitor the working hours being served by the subordinate staff and in case of nonconformity; necessary steps should be taken for its adaptation. As per policy: “School staff shall report for duty in Branches as per the following: Staff Time In Time Out Teachers on duty 30 minutes before school starts 30 minutes after school ends Admin & Office staff 8 working hours Determined by RO All the employees’ files should be complete and updated. According to policy: “A detailed check list is attached as Annexure-3-P. This check list shall be pasted in the inner side of the file. Branch Head shall ensure that all the required documents are filed in personal files of employees as per the check list pasted in the file”. Approval for relative employees should be taken from competent authority. As per policy: “Blood relations and related family members (including husband, wife, parents, son, daughter, brother, sister, grandparent, grandchild, brother-in-law, sister-in-law, father-in-law, mother-in-law, son-in-law and daughter in-law) can only be hired in the same branch or office with the approval of the Head of HR (HHR). However, under no circumstances shall one be allowed to be in a supervisory capacity over the other, or at a position giving rise to a situation resulting in conflict of interest. Similarly, if one employee marries another, both may retain their positions provided neither is in a supervisory/influential capacity over the other. In case of concealment in any of the aforesaid situations, the Organization may take appropriate action.” Appropriate procedure should be devised and adopted at concerned levels regarding; ➢ Registration of employees. ➢ PESSI record-keeping (for instance PESSI Employee Cards). ➢ PESSI cards issued to the junior staff. Employees should also be informed about the benefits provided by PESSI for example medical care facilities and cash benefits to the secured workers and their dependents. Branch Head should ensure compliance to the company policies. The Branch accountant should keep a keen eye on these while preparations of salary. As per policy: “Off days or gazetted holidays falling in between leave periods (sandwiched) shall be counted as part of that leave. For example, if leave is applied for on a Friday and Monday, then Saturday and Sunday will be included in the leave”. Care should be taken while processing the payroll. Excessive amount should be collected from the concerned employee with the coordination of HR. Branch Head should ensure that all the receipts are deposited on timely basis. As per policy: “Cash collected as registration fee shall be deposited in the main bank account designated for collection, by close of every working week. However, in cases where the collection exceeds PKR 10,000/- the same must be deposited immediately.” Branch Head should ensure that all the receipts and deposited are correctly fed in the system. Complete information should be updated in BEAMS at an early basis. As per policy: “The PRO and Accountant shall enter Student information in Integrated Student Module (ISM) respectively at the time of admission;” Reason for the waiver in Registration fee should be mentioned in the BEAMS. Missing fixed assets should be located by the branch. As Policy: “Following authorities shall be responsible for the safe custody of the assets of the Company: Principals/Branch Heads for their respective schools”. All the Fixed Assets should be numbered as per Fixed Asset Register. As per Policy: “Upon receipt of codes, Designated Officer of User Office shall affix these codes on respective fixed assets immediately. Such codes shall be affixed in a systematic and permanent manner”. All the Fixed Assets should be numbered as per Fixed Asset Register. As per Policy: “Upon receipt of codes, Designated Officer of User Office shall affix these codes on respective fixed assets immediately. Such codes shall be affixed in a systematic and permanent manner”. All required Stocks should be entered in the Register Physical Balance should be matched with the records. Register should be validated by the Branch Head regularly. In order to keep track of annual paint work expense, branch should have an updated record of paint area measurement duly endorsed by RO. Keeping in view the level of students, the quantity of books should be increased. As per Regional Librarian, “the standard ratio is 15 books per student.” File should be prepared and updated on timely according to Policy: “If a person left the system with outstanding books/library items, it should be mentioned on clearance form and keep record properly”. Librarian should maintain the minutes file for reference as per Policy: “The Regional Librarian should call a meeting once/twice in an academic year of school librarians. All librarians are given minutes of that meeting. The librarian should file these.” Reminders should be issued for the books that are overdue and a file should be maintained for record. As per policy: “A file should be maintained with a copy of the Reminders issued to the teachers/students for not returning the books on time” Library books should be returned back according to company’s policy. As per Library Rules in Library Manual Page 21, Clause 10: “Books should not be issued for more than a week”. Keeping in view the importance of above-mentioned features which are already available in existing open source library module (KOHA), there is a need to ensure to access and practice of these options for the more controlled, efficient, accurate and scrutinized working of branch librarians by utilizing the available resources. Assembly area should be clearly labelled as per the emergency plan of branch in order to ensure smooth evacuation. At least 15 days backup time should be maintained for security purposes. As per Security Guidelines of BSS Pakistan, Clause 3D “Keep CCTV Recording/Tape for 15 days at least.” The rear gate should always be closed and should only be opened after specific caution by the security staff positioned inside the screening room. As per Chapter-4, “Charter of Duties” of Security guidelines “SOP for the New Security Paradigm” stating common duties of Chowkidar (School Guard): “Lady Searcher will knock the inner door with preset signal for Chowkidar to open and an escort from school to lead the visitor to the visited person.” Fifty percent of total guard should be retired army man, according to the contract; “Deploy well trained armed guards preferably retired from military with 50% civil/military ratio.” Generator Log book record should be updated monthly by Branch OFA and Branch Head. As per policy “Officer Facility Administration (OFA) / Administration Officer (AO) shall maintain the record (logbook & invoices) pertinent to generator operations including fuelling for their respective Branches / Offices. Following information shall be recorded in the logbook on daily basis: Date & time of diesel re-filling Quantity of fuel filled Meter readings before and after the fuelling Running hours of generator and time Fuel average Replacement of parts, if any Detail of other maintenance activities e.g. change of engine oil, fuel filter, air filter etc.” Demolition register should be maintained by branch for scrap. As per policy: “A demolition register shall be maintained at the Branch by the Caretaker or designated person, and should be vetted by the BH and RMO.” Physical Stock should be matched with the records. Register should be validated by Branch Head on regular intervals. As per policy: Stock Register Maintained BY Checked By BH Printed Stationery should be validated by Designated Official, Quarterly. Physical Stock should be matched with the records. Register should be validated by Branch Head on regular intervals. As per policy: Stock Register Maintained BY Checked By BH Sports Register should be validated by Designated Official, Quarterly.

Short Office Hours Branch Head should ensure that complete office hours are being followed by the employees. During sample-based review of employee attendance, it was revealed that some of the branch staff was not following the official timings. The matter may affect operational efficiency of the Branch and also the leave encashment and salary of respective staff. Some of the instances are attached as Annexure-I. Next time we can monitor this as per the BSS Policy. Incomplete Employees’ Files Employees’ files should be completed in all respects. During checking of files during the audit it was observed that some documents like; Nomination Form, CV, Confirmation Letter & Attested Certificates etc., were missing in them as well. Instances are mentioned in Annexure-J. Next time we will be more vigilant. Related Family Employees Working in the Branch As per company policy, blood and related family members can be hired in a branch with approval of HHR. However, during random review of files we came to know of a case in which blood relatives and related family members were working in a branch against which approval of HHR was not provided/available. Moreover, branch was not maintaining any record of blood and related family members working in the same premises or otherwise. Detail of identified blood relatives is attached below; Sr. # Name Designation Relation 1 Mr. Huraira Lab Attendant Brothers 2 Mr. Hamza Assistant Accountant Above stated employees fall under the category as informed by branch personnel. Necessary action has been taken as per BSS Policy. It was verified in the subsequent audit visit that Disclosure form has been submitted by the concerned employee. Employees Record of Social Security not Available As per Punjab Govt directions, employees having salary from Rs. 17,500 to Rs 22,000 (or as prescribed by the notification issued time to time) should be registered with Punjab Employees Social Security Institution (providing hospitalization and dispensary facilities etc.) We observed that PESSI record (including copy of PESSI data form/card) of junior staff was not available and the PESSI Cards were also not issued to the Junior staff. We will start working on it. Sandwich Leaves not Considered As per BSS policies, any gazetted/official leaves that are sandwiched between the employees’ leaves will be accounted for as part of leaves and hence will be charged to the employee. During scrutiny of attendance record we found a case where sandwich leaves were not accounted for. Details are mentioned below: Employee ID Employee Name Leave Before Off Day Leave Type Off Day(s) Leave After Off Day Leave Type 86389 Nimra Asif Khan 05/08/2022 Sick Leave 06/08/2022 - 09/08/2022 10/08/2022 Long Leave She was a Transfer employee from JTC Junior Campus. She joined our campus on August 1st, 2024. Excess Salary Paid to Employee Due care should be exercised while making/transferring the salaries of employees. Any excess Payments should be reverted back/recovered from concerned staff on timely basis. It was observed during the audit that excess salary was paid to Ms. Mahnoor Rana (Teacher) for the m/o May 2022 for 7 days amounting to Rs.9,065/- Further leave Encashment was paid in double, once during regular payment of the Leave Encashment and secondly at the time of final settlement dues, amounting to Rs.2,914/- This case was wrongly done by the previous Accountant Mahnoor Rana. Leave encashment amount of Rs 2,914/- was system generated, same amount was also deducted in the Final settlement calculation. Salary reversals should be done through branch in a timely manner. Registration Fee Deposited with Delay As per Company Policy registration fee should be deposited on weekly basis or immediately where the amount of registration fee collection reaches PKR 10,000/- or more. Delays were observed while checking registration fee record. Instances are mentioned as Annexure-K. We will be more vigilant in the future. Registration Fee Deposited prior to the Collection As per Company Policy Registration fee collected should be deposited on weekly basis. It was observed during the audit that in BEAMS certain registration fee collections were deposited prior to their collection dates. Apparently, the deposit dates were wrongly fed by the concerned person. Instances are mentioned as Annexure-L. This happened mistakenly. In the future, we will be more careful. Emergency Contact Information of Students not Mentioned in BEAMS Student data should be updated at the time of feeding admission information of student. The emergency contact numbers are updated on Beams. Reason for Registration Fee Waiver not Mentioned Student Registration data should be complete in all respect. It was observed during the audit that the reason for Free Registration was not mentioned in the BEAMS Registration Register. Instances are mentioned as Annexure-N. This happened mistakenly. Asset IDs have been affixed on the above assets (as mentioned by auditee). During physical verification of assets, on sample basis, some double-numbered assets were observed in the Branch. Detail of instances are mentioned in Annexure-P. Certain Stocks were not entered in the Register Physical Balance not matched with the records. Register was not validated by the Branch Head regularly. It's Done. It was observed that total paintable area of branch duly endorsed by group school improvement officer was not available with branch. We will update the record. Low per Child Book Ratio in Library All libraries should have a sufficient quantity of library books. In Middle Library, the item per child ratio was low as 7.19 and 6.73 in 2023 and 2024 respectively. The standard book ratio as decided by the Director of Studies is 15 books per child. I have already informed the ROC about the low per-child book ratio and have requested an increase in the library budget to fulfil the required number of items. File of Clearance Forms not Maintained File of Clearance Forms should be maintained by the branch. During audit it was observed that file Clearance Forms of Withdrawn Students and Left Employees was not prepared by the branch. The Student Clearance forms were not submitted, which is why we were unable to maintain such files. However, we have now informed the concerned departments to follow the proper procedure, and the files will be maintained accordingly moving forward. File for Minutes of Library Coordination Meeting not Maintained Minutes of the librarian meeting with RO Librarian should be filed by branch librarian. During the audit it was observed that minutes of librarian meeting was not filed in Library files. The Minutes of Librarian Meeting file was not in practice before my joining, but moving forward, we will ensure that Minutes of Librarian Meeting file are maintained as per the required procedure. File for Reminders not Maintained Reminders should be issued to the person who fail to submit the issued books on time to library. A file should be kept as a record for the reminders issued. It was observed that no file for reminders was maintained in library. Reminders are given through Google Classroom or email by the English teacher. The file was not maintained previously because all communication and submissions were online. However, keeping the current requirements in mind, we will now create and maintain the file accordingly. Overdue Books Books issued, should be returned within stipulated time. It was observed during the audit that some students/teachers did not return the library books. Details are mentioned in Annexure-Q. The books issued to teaching staff are overdue because they require them for the entire term. On the other hand, the overdue books issued to students are those where the withdrawal was not communicated, and now we are unable to contact the students. Discrepancies in Library Module (KOHA) Efficient utilization of library software (KOHA) should be ensured. Following discrepancies were observed and subsequently confirmed by the branch librarian in discussion which seemed to be creating difficulties for the librarians in performing their day to day operations regarding library module; ❖ For branch librarian rights to view & access books were not restricted to specific branch. ❖ Auto generation of Over-due books notification (email) was not in practice. ❖ Auto generation of Issued & Returned books notification (email) was not in practice. ❖ Stocktaking through bar codes and subsequently stocktaking report generation. There is no auto-generation of Over-due & Issued & Returned books notifications. Reminders are given through Google Classroom or email Assembly area Unmarked Emergency exits and Assembly areas should be clearly marked ensuring smooth evacuation of buildings. In-effective Screening Room Screening room should be properly closed and locked from both sides to ensure that any visitor can only enter the building once cleared by the security staff. Only at home time when our other doors are operational for student disbursement, the guards are engaged in other doors. They are reminded frequently about the provision of ex-military guards as prescribed in the agreement. School security should not be compromised at the expense of penalty charges.
