observations.title: Open Activities against Students’ Cash Collections
observations.description: Every Beams generated student activity should be closed right after the end of the activity. During the audit it was observed that bonfire activity is still unclosed in BEAMS. Details as mentioned as below: Activity Start Date Activity End Date Activity Name Total Collection Total Expense Balance Activity Status 12/12/2024 24/12/2024 Extracurricular Activity - Bonfire (12-DEC-2024 - 24-DEC-2024) Rs.79,500 Rs.79,500 Open
observations.recommendation: Activities that are still marked as "Open" but have been completed, must be closed in BEAMS. The Branch Accountant is required to close each activity upon its completion and submit a monthly summary of receipts and expenses to the Branch Head.
observations.auditee_response: Next time we will take care of it. Instructed to the lead Accountant for strict future compliance, and also instructed to close the activity as soon as possible. Recruitment, Payroll & Employees’ Record

observations.title: Delay in Confirmation of Employees
observations.description: Employees should be confirmed after completion of probationary period and their confirmation letters issued without any delay. In case, if the branch management needs to extend the probation period, it should be communicated to the concerned employee through probation extension letter. During audit it was observed that confirmation letter of few employees was issued with certain delays. Further, no intimation of extension of probation period was made to the concerned employees by the branch management. Following are the delays observed: ID Name Designation Category Hire Date Confirm Date Delay Months 93554 Fasiha Batool Teacher Teaching Staff 07/11/2022 01/08/2023 1 92048 Safia Tariq Housekeeping Attendant Support Staff 18/08/2022 01/04/2023 1 85979 Mubashar Abbas Teacher P.E. / Games Teaching Staff 09/08/2021 09/03/2022 1 86024 Tehreem Ishtiaq Teacher Teaching Staff 09/08/2021 09/03/2022 1 95148 Saba Pervez Teacher Teaching Staff 09/03/2023 01/01/2024 2
observations.recommendation: Probation period should not be un-necessarily prolonged and the office order for the confirmation of services should be issued on timely basis. However, in case of extension in the probation period, office order for such extension should be issued to the concerned employee. As per policy: “Unless otherwise stated in the contract of employment, all employees are required to undergo a probationary period of six (06) working months. In case of unsatisfactory performance, the Line Manager may extend probation period for an additional three (03) months.”
observations.auditee_response: Refer to ROC. Confirmation extensions were processed upon recommendation of Head of School and duly shared as well.

observations.title: Short Office Hours
observations.description: Branch Head should ensure that complete office hours are being followed by the employees. During sample-based review of employee attendance, it was revealed that some of the branch staff was not following the official timings. The matter may affect operational efficiency of the Branch and also the leave encashment and salary of respective staff. Some of the instances are attached as Annexure-I.
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should monitor the working hours being served by the subordinate staff and in case of nonconformity; necessary steps should be taken for its adaptation. As per policy: “School staff shall report for duty in Branches as per the following: Staff Time In Time Out Teachers on duty 30 minutes before school starts 30 minutes after school ends Admin & Office staff 8 working hours Determined by RO
observations.auditee_response: Next time we can monitor this as per the BSS Policy.

observations.title: Incomplete Employees’ Files
observations.description: Employees’ files should be completed in all respects. During checking of files during the audit it was observed that some documents like; Nomination Form, CV, Confirmation Letter & Attested Certificates etc., were missing in them as well. Instances are mentioned in Annexure-J.
observations.recommendation: All the employees’ files should be complete and updated. According to policy: “A detailed check list is attached as Annexure-3-P. This check list shall be pasted in the inner side of the file. Branch Head shall ensure that all the required documents are filed in personal files of employees as per the check list pasted in the file”.
observations.auditee_response: Next time we will be more vigilant.

observations.title: Related Family Employees Working in the Branch
observations.description: As per company policy, blood and related family members can be hired in a branch with approval of HHR. However, during random review of files we came to know of a case in which blood relatives and related family members were working in a branch against which approval of HHR was not provided/available. Moreover, branch was not maintaining any record of blood and related family members working in the same premises or otherwise. Detail of identified blood relatives is attached below; Sr. # Name Designation Relation 1 Mr. Huraira Lab Attendant Brothers 2 Mr. Hamza Assistant Accountant Above stated employees fall under the category as informed by branch personnel.
observations.recommendation: Approval for relative employees should be taken from competent authority. As per policy: “Blood relations and related family members (including husband, wife, parents, son, daughter, brother, sister, grandparent, grandchild, brother-in-law, sister-in-law, father-in-law, mother-in-law, son-in-law and daughter in-law) can only be hired in the same branch or office with the approval of the Head of HR (HHR). However, under no circumstances shall one be allowed to be in a supervisory capacity over the other, or at a position giving rise to a situation resulting in conflict of interest. Similarly, if one employee marries another, both may retain their positions provided neither is in a supervisory/influential capacity over the other. In case of concealment in any of the aforesaid situations, the Organization may take appropriate action.”
observations.auditee_response: Necessary action has been taken as per BSS Policy. It was verified in the subsequent audit visit that Disclosure form has been submitted by the concerned employee.

observations.title: Employees Record of Social Security not Available
observations.description: As per Punjab Govt directions, employees having salary from Rs. 17,500 to Rs 22,000 (or as prescribed by the notification issued time to time) should be registered with Punjab Employees Social Security Institution (providing hospitalization and dispensary facilities etc.) We observed that PESSI record (including copy of PESSI data form/card) of junior staff was not available and the PESSI Cards were also not issued to the Junior staff.
observations.recommendation: Appropriate procedure should be devised and adopted at concerned levels regarding; ➢ Registration of employees. ➢ PESSI record-keeping (for instance PESSI Employee Cards). ➢ PESSI cards issued to the junior staff. Employees should also be informed about the benefits provided by PESSI for example medical care facilities and cash benefits to the secured workers and their dependents.
observations.auditee_response: We will start working on it.

observations.title: Sandwich Leaves not Considered
observations.description: As per BSS policies, any gazetted/official leaves that are sandwiched between the employees’ leaves will be accounted for as part of leaves and hence will be charged to the employee. During scrutiny of attendance record we found a case where sandwich leaves were not accounted for. Details are mentioned below: Employee ID Employee Name Leave Before Off Day Leave Type Off Day(s) Leave After Off Day Leave Type 86389 Nimra Asif Khan 05/08/2022 Sick Leave 06/08/2022 - 09/08/2022 10/08/2022 Long Leave
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should ensure compliance to the company policies. The Branch accountant should keep a keen eye on these while preparations of salary. As per policy: “Off days or gazetted holidays falling in between leave periods (sandwiched) shall be counted as part of that leave. For example, if leave is applied for on a Friday and Monday, then Saturday and Sunday will be included in the leave”.
observations.auditee_response: She was a Transfer employee from JTC Junior Campus. She joined our campus on August 1st, 2024.

observations.title: Excess Salary Paid to Employee
observations.description: Due care should be exercised while making/transferring the salaries of employees. Any excess Payments should be reverted back/recovered from concerned staff on timely basis. It was observed during the audit that excess salary was paid to Ms. Mahnoor Rana (Teacher) for the m/o May 2022 for 7 days amounting to Rs.9,065/- Further leave Encashment was paid in double, once during regular payment of the Leave Encashment and secondly at the time of final settlement dues, amounting to Rs.2,914/-
observations.recommendation: Care should be taken while processing the payroll. Excessive amount should be collected from the concerned employee with the coordination of HR.
observations.auditee_response: This case was wrongly done by the previous Accountant Mahnoor Rana. Leave encashment amount of Rs 2,914/- was system generated, same amount was also deducted in the Final settlement calculation. Salary reversals should be done through branch in a timely manner.

observations.title: Registration Fee Deposited with Delay
observations.description: As per Company Policy registration fee should be deposited on weekly basis or immediately where the amount of registration fee collection reaches PKR 10,000/- or more. Delays were observed while checking registration fee record. Instances are mentioned as Annexure-K.
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should ensure that all the receipts are deposited on timely basis. As per policy: “Cash collected as registration fee shall be deposited in the main bank account designated for collection, by close of every working week. However, in cases where the collection exceeds PKR 10,000/- the same must be deposited immediately.”
observations.auditee_response: We will be more vigilant in the future.

observations.title: Registration Fee Deposited prior to the Collection
observations.description: As per Company Policy Registration fee collected should be deposited on weekly basis. It was observed during the audit that in BEAMS certain registration fee collections were deposited prior to their collection dates. Apparently, the deposit dates were wrongly fed by the concerned person. Instances are mentioned as Annexure-L.
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should ensure that all the receipts and deposited are correctly fed in the system.
observations.auditee_response: This happened mistakenly. In the future, we will be more careful.

observations.title: Emergency Contact Information of Students not Mentioned in BEAMS
observations.description: Student data should be updated at the time of feeding admission information of student. During scrutiny of student record on BEAMS in current audit, it was found that data of students i.e. emergency contact number was not entered in BEAMS. Few instances are given in Annexure-M.
observations.recommendation: Complete information should be updated in BEAMS at an early basis. As per policy: “The PRO and Accountant shall enter Student information in Integrated Student Module (ISM) respectively at the time of admission;”
observations.auditee_response: The emergency contact numbers are updated on Beams.

observations.title: Reason for Registration Fee Waiver not Mentioned
observations.description: Student Registration data should be complete in all respect. It was observed during the audit that the reason for Free Registration was not mentioned in the BEAMS Registration Register. Instances are mentioned as Annexure-N.
observations.recommendation: Reason for the waiver in Registration fee should be mentioned in the BEAMS.
observations.auditee_response: This happened mistakenly. In the future, we will be more careful.

observations.title: Fixed Assets Remained Untraced
observations.description: Fixed assets represent considerable investment and therefore due care is needed for their use and safety. School Head is required to ensure the safe custody of fixed assets as per the company policy. During current audit, some of the assets appearing in the Fixed Assets Register could not be located by the concerned staff of branch. Detail of instances is as follows: Sr. No. Assets # Assets Name 1 446052 Computer CPU 2 229764 Computer CPU 3 446056 Computer CPU 4 432296 Hub Switch 5 331654 Monitor LCD
observations.recommendation: Missing fixed assets should be located by the branch. As Policy: “Following authorities shall be responsible for the safe custody of the assets of the Company: Principals/Branch Heads for their respective schools”.
observations.auditee_response: Above mention, Assets are available in the Campus.

observations.title: Unnumbered Assets
observations.description: All the Fixed Assets should be numbered with the Codes assigned to them. During physical verification of assets, on sample basis, some un-numbered assets were observed in the Branch. Detail of instances are mentioned in Annexure-O.
observations.recommendation: All the Fixed Assets should be numbered as per Fixed Asset Register. As per Policy: “Upon receipt of codes, Designated Officer of User Office shall affix these codes on respective fixed assets immediately. Such codes shall be affixed in a systematic and permanent manner”.
observations.auditee_response: Numbers are mentioned on the Motor Bike, Water motor pump, Walkie & Talkie and Hub Switch further items are Referred to ROC and AMCO. Asset IDs have been affixed on the above assets (as mentioned by auditee). However, QR tags are placed on the Chromebooks, and these will be mapped with the asset IDs in future and displayed in the FAR.

observations.title: Duplicate Numbers of Assets
observations.description: All the Fixed Assets should be numbered with the Codes assigned to them. During physical verification of assets, on sample basis, some double-numbered assets were observed in the Branch. Detail of instances are mentioned in Annexure-P.
observations.recommendation: All the Fixed Assets should be numbered as per Fixed Asset Register. As per Policy: “Upon receipt of codes, Designated Officer of User Office shall affix these codes on respective fixed assets immediately. Such codes shall be affixed in a systematic and permanent manner”.
observations.auditee_response: Correct Numbers are mentioned on UPS and Bar Code Reader. And Router referred to AMCO.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Memorandum Record of Fixed Assets
observations.description: Memorandum record should be maintained by the branch as mentioned in the policies. During audit certain discrepancies were observed in the maintenance of memorandum records of fixed assets. Certain Stocks were not entered in the Register Physical Balance not matched with the records. Register was not validated by the Branch Head regularly.
observations.recommendation: All required Stocks should be entered in the Register Physical Balance should be matched with the records. Register should be validated by the Branch Head regularly.
observations.auditee_response: It's Done.

observations.title: Validated Paint Area Measurements not Available
observations.description: As paint work is a regular yearly exercise in the branch, record of paint area measurement should be available in the branch to avoid any ambiguity at the time of awarding paint work contracts. It was observed that total paintable area of branch duly endorsed by group school improvement officer was not available with branch.
observations.recommendation: In order to keep track of annual paint work expense, branch should have an updated record of paint area measurement duly endorsed by RO.
observations.auditee_response: We will update the record.

observations.title: Low per Child Book Ratio in Library
observations.description: All libraries should have a sufficient quantity of library books. In Middle Library, the item per child ratio was low as 7.19 and 6.73 in 2023 and 2024 respectively. The standard book ratio as decided by the Director of Studies is 15 books per child.
observations.recommendation: Keeping in view the level of students, the quantity of books should be increased. As per Regional Librarian, “the standard ratio is 15 books per student.”
observations.auditee_response: I have already informed the ROC about the low per-child book ratio and have requested an increase in the library budget to fulfil the required number of items.

observations.title: File of Clearance Forms not Maintained
observations.description: File of Clearance Forms should be maintained by the branch. During audit it was observed that file Clearance Forms of Withdrawn Students and Left Employees was not prepared by the branch.
observations.recommendation: File should be prepared and updated on timely according to Policy: “If a person left the system with outstanding books/library items, it should be mentioned on clearance form and keep record properly”. Librarian should maintain the minutes file for reference as per Policy: “The Regional Librarian should call a meeting once/twice in an academic year of school librarians. All librarians are given minutes of that meeting. The librarian should file these.”
observations.auditee_response: The Student Clearance forms were not submitted, which is why we were unable to maintain such files. However, we have now informed the concerned departments to follow the proper procedure, and the files will be maintained accordingly moving forward. File for Minutes of Library Coordination Meeting not Maintained Minutes of the librarian meeting with RO Librarian should be filed by branch librarian. During the audit it was observed that minutes of librarian meeting was not filed in Library files. The Minutes of Librarian Meeting file was not in practice before my joining, but moving forward, we will ensure that Minutes of Librarian Meeting file are maintained as per the required procedure.

observations.title: File for Reminders not Maintained
observations.description: Reminders should be issued to the person who fail to submit the issued books on time to library. A file should be kept as a record for the reminders issued. It was observed that no file for reminders was maintained in library.
observations.recommendation: Reminders should be issued for the books that are overdue and a file should be maintained for record. As per policy: “A file should be maintained with a copy of the Reminders issued to the teachers/students for not returning the books on time”
observations.auditee_response: Reminders are given through Google Classroom or email by the English teacher. The file was not maintained previously because all communication and submissions were online. However, keeping the current requirements in mind, we will now create and maintain the file accordingly.

observations.title: Overdue Books
observations.description: Books issued, should be returned within stipulated time. It was observed during the audit that some students/teachers did not return the library books. Details are mentioned in Annexure-Q.
observations.recommendation: Library books should be returned back according to company’s policy. As per Library Rules in Library Manual Page 21, Clause 10: “Books should not be issued for more than a week”.
observations.auditee_response: The books issued to teaching staff are overdue because they require them for the entire term. On the other hand, the overdue books issued to students are those where the withdrawal was not communicated, and now we are unable to contact the students.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Library Module (KOHA)
observations.description: Efficient utilization of library software (KOHA) should be ensured. Following discrepancies were observed and subsequently confirmed by the branch librarian in discussion which seemed to be creating difficulties for the librarians in performing their day to day operations regarding library module; ❖ For branch librarian rights to view & access books were not restricted to specific branch. ❖ Auto generation of Over-due books notification (email) was not in practice. ❖ Auto generation of Issued & Returned books notification (email) was not in practice. ❖ Stocktaking through bar codes and subsequently stocktaking report generation.
observations.recommendation: Keeping in view the importance of above-mentioned features which are already available in existing open source library module (KOHA), there is a need to ensure to access and practice of these options for the more controlled, efficient, accurate and scrutinized working of branch librarians by utilizing the available resources.
observations.auditee_response: There is no auto-generation of Over-due & Issued & Returned books notifications. Reminders are given through Google Classroom or email

observations.title: Assembly area Unmarked
observations.description: Emergency exits and Assembly areas should be clearly marked ensuring smooth evacuation of buildings. It was observed that “assembly area” were labelled in branch. Further the allocation of designated assembly area for specific group of students were not marked such as Early Year Section, Middle Section, etc.
observations.recommendation: Assembly area should be clearly labelled as per the emergency plan of branch in order to ensure smooth evacuation.
observations.auditee_response: We are working on it.

observations.title: Insufficient Backup time of CCTV Cameras
observations.description: Sufficient back up time of CCTV Cameras should be available for better security controls. It was observed during current audit that there was 10 days backup time of one DVRs having 16 CCTV cameras.
observations.recommendation: At least 15 days backup time should be maintained for security purposes. As per Security Guidelines of BSS Pakistan, Clause 3D “Keep CCTV Recording/Tape for 15 days at least.”
observations.auditee_response: Issue resolved. It was verified in the subsequent audit visit that sufficient backup facility is available for CCTV recording.

observations.title: In-effective Screening Room
observations.description: Screening room should be properly closed and locked from both sides to ensure that any visitor can only enter the building once cleared by the security staff. During audit it was noted that screening room function was in-effective as rear door was always open.
observations.recommendation: The rear gate should always be closed and should only be opened after specific caution by the security staff positioned inside the screening room. As per Chapter-4, “Charter of Duties” of Security guidelines “SOP for the New Security Paradigm” stating common duties of Chowkidar (School Guard): “Lady Searcher will knock the inner door with preset signal for Chowkidar to open and an escort from school to lead the visitor to the visited person.” Fifty percent of total guard should be retired army man, according to the contract; “Deploy well trained armed guards preferably retired from military with 50% civil/military ratio.”
observations.auditee_response: Maximum times our screening room door is closed as per the Security SOP. Only at home time when our other doors are operational for student disbursement, the guards are engaged in other doors. Non Compliance of Contract for Security Guards Security Company should provide armed guard from retired soldiers according to the ratio agreed upon in the agreement. During audit it was observed that 4 guard were deputed by the Security Company and all of them were civilians. It has mentioned the security company many times. We will further communicate to the Security Company H.O for future compliance. Monetary penalties are charged to the vendor in the monthly bill against non-provision of ex-military guards. They are reminded frequently about the provision of ex-military guards as prescribed in the agreement. School security should not be compromised at the expense of penalty charges.

observations.title: Incomplete Generator Log Book
observations.description: Generator Log book should be prepared, maintained and signed by the generator operator and caretaker. During audit, it was observed that the Log Book was not maintained as per directives. Following objections were observed in this regard: No details of maintenance activities. No meter Reading mentioned. No fuel average calculated.
observations.recommendation: Generator Log book record should be updated monthly by Branch OFA and Branch Head. As per policy “Officer Facility Administration (OFA) / Administration Officer (AO) shall maintain the record (logbook & invoices) pertinent to generator operations including fuelling for their respective Branches / Offices. Following information shall be recorded in the logbook on daily basis: Date & time of diesel re-filling Quantity of fuel filled Meter readings before and after the fuelling Running hours of generator and time Fuel average Replacement of parts, if any Detail of other maintenance activities e.g. change of engine oil, fuel filter, air filter etc.”
observations.auditee_response: The Generator maintenance file is separately maintained. And only Fuel averages are missing. We will complete it as soon as possible.

observations.title: Demolition Register Not Maintained
observations.description: As per policy, a demolition register shall be maintained for scrap obtained as a result of demolition. It was observed that demolition register was not maintained at branch.
observations.recommendation: Demolition register should be maintained by branch for scrap. As per policy: “A demolition register shall be maintained at the Branch by the Caretaker or designated person, and should be vetted by the BH and RMO.”
observations.auditee_response: As per your recommendation, the New Register will be maintained.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Maintaining Printed Stationery Register
observations.description: All stock registers should be maintained properly as per company policies. During audit it was observed that Printed Stationery Register was not maintained by the branch as per policy. Following are the discrepancies observed: Physical stock was not matching with the records. Register was not validated by branch Head on regular basis
observations.recommendation: Physical Stock should be matched with the records. Register should be validated by Branch Head on regular intervals. As per policy: Stock Register Maintained BY Checked By BH Printed Stationery should be validated by Designated Official, Quarterly.
observations.auditee_response: Printed Stationery register were physically verified by OFA and then signed by the Principal. It was verified in the subsequent audit visit that Printed Stationery Register was maintained as per recommendations.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Maintaining Sports Register
observations.description: All stock registers should be maintained properly as per company policies. During audit it was observed that Sports Register was not maintained by the branch as per policy. Following are the discrepancies observed: Physical Stock was not matching with the records. Register was not validated by branch Head on regular basis
observations.recommendation: Physical Stock should be matched with the records. Register should be validated by Branch Head on regular intervals. As per policy: Stock Register Maintained BY Checked By BH Sports Register should be validated by Designated Official, Quarterly.
observations.auditee_response: Sports registers were physically verified by OFA and then signed by the Principal. It was verified in the subsequent audit visit that Sports Register was maintained as per recommendations. observations.title: Expenditure Exceeded the Budgeted Amount
observations.description: Budgetary limits for each expense head should be kept in view while making expenditure. The review of system generated “Budget Variance Sheets” revealed that significant overspending was made under different heads of accounts, for the year 2020-21, 2021-22, 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. Detail of unfavourable variances (account head wise), is attached as Annexure-A.
observations.recommendation: The overspending should be controlled/monitored by Branch Head. Efforts should be made to spend budgeted amounts in accordance with their allocation. According to Policy: “Budget variance shall be monitored for judicious use of funds allocated under all heads of expenses. The system generated budget variance sheet should be consulted to monitor variance of expense against budget allocation and discrepancies, if any, rectified.” Imprest budget should be monitored by ROC on monthly basis. According to policy: “Monitoring of imprest budget variances of Branches shall be conducted monthly at the RO”
observations.auditee_response: We will review the noted overspending under the respective heads of accounts and ensure that proper checks and controls are implemented to prevent such variances in the future. But sometimes there are unforeseen expenses occurred which causes these negative variances.

observations.title: Savings in Student Expenditure
observations.description: As per Company policy, savings under the category of student expenses should be avoided. During review of “Budget Variance Sheets”, it was observed that budget for student expenditure remained un-utilized in certain heads of student expenses, for the year 2020-21, 2021-22, 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25. The detail is attached as Annexure-B.
observations.recommendation: Budget for student expenses should be fully utilized and savings in these heads of accounts should be avoided. As per policy: “There should be no saving of funds under the category of “student expenses”.
observations.auditee_response: We acknowledge that certain student expense heads remained unutilized during the years 2020-21 to 2024-25, as reflected in the Budget Variance Sheets. We will review these areas in detail to identify the causes of underutilization and take corrective measures to ensure proper and timely utilization of the allocated student budget in the future.

observations.title: Delay in Deposit of Withholding Tax
observations.recommendation: Tax policies should be strictly followed; any lapses in this regard may result in penalties to the company. As per DF letter number 10597 dated January 27, 2011: “Please follow the instructions at your end and also instruct the schools and other concerned staff to deduct the tax accordingly and Deposit the tax into Government Treasury within seven days from the deduction and payment”.
observations.auditee_response: We have noted the instances where delays occurred in depositing the tax on payments made to suppliers/vendors. We will review the underlying causes of these delays and ensure that corrective measures are implemented so that all future Withholding Tax deposits are made within the prescribed timelines.

observations.title: Delayed Reimbursement of Claims by RO
observations.description: Branch is being allocated limited budget against each head of account, late reimbursements to the Branch may lead to shortage of funds for smooth execution of operations. During current audit, some instances were observed where reimbursements were finalized/disbursed with significant delays to the Branch by ROC. For detail, please refer to Annexure-C.
observations.recommendation: To avoid unnecessary delays and shortage of funds in branch, reimbursement claims should be processed on timely basis by ROC. As per Policy: “All reimbursement claims received shall be checked by respective Accounts department within 20 days of their receipt”. Referred to Regional Office
observations.auditee_response: Refer to ROC Please be informed that ROC Finance handles branch reimbursement cases in a systematic manner, prioritizing them among other tasks. As a result, we cannot commit to a 20-day completion timeline, as this is not consistently achievable. Below are a few factors that cause deviations from the 20-day timeline. Some bills are based on purchase orders (POs) and are forwarded to the relevant departments (Procurement, Marketing, Construction) for PO generation, which takes additional processing time. Certain bills are received late from branches due to delays in completing the related activities and engagement in urgent tasks. Sometimes, priority items at desk is another factor of late processing the claims. Furthermore, in practical scenarios, the 20-day timeline is often insufficient for the majority of cases. Timelines mention in the policies & procedures should be followed by all the Departments, However, if the timelines are not practicable, those should be amended through proper procedure.

observations.title: Vendors Registration not Completed
observations.description: Process of vendor registration should be completed in due course. Record of all the registered vendors should be available for verification. Whereas it was observed that record of “Registered Vendors”, such as Vendors Registration Application (VRA) Forms, VRF and supporting documents were not available. It was informed by the Accountant that no registration of vendors were made since her joining in the Campus (September 2023)
observations.recommendation: As per policy: 1, “The procurement shall be made from registered vendors. The registered vendor is a vendor who is enrolled in Vendor Register of that Branch, based on approved VRF.” 2, “The BA or designated member of BPC shall complete the VRF, based on the criteria detailed above and sign the completed form. VRA, VRF and related documents, if any, shall be forwarded to BH for approval.” 3, “BH shall review the documents submitted and provide approval on VRF for inclusion in Vendor Register, upon satisfaction.” 4, “AMCO shall ensure that the particulars of vendor have been entered in Vendor Register as registered vendor and notify the vendor thereof in writing.” 5, “BH shall review and ensure periodically that the Vendor Register is being maintained and updated effectively on regular basis. Such review shall be conducted at least once in a calendar year.”
observations.auditee_response: We will review this lapse immediately and ensure that the vendor registration process is reinitiated and documentation for all active vendors is completed and properly filed. Measures will be taken to maintain updated and accessible records.

observations.title: List of Common Suppliers not Available in the Branch
observations.description: List of common suppliers should be available in the branch for the deduction of income tax. It was observed during the audit that list of common supplier’s f/y 2025-26 was not available in the branch.
observations.recommendation: List of common suppliers should be timely provided by RO for the deduction of withholding tax.
observations.auditee_response: Refer to ROC Already shared with the AMCO. It was verified during subsequent audit visit that the list of common supplier was received from Regional office.

observations.title: Purchase Committee not Properly Functioning
observations.description: As per policy, Purchase Committee (PC) members should be actively involved in overseeing and execution of procurement related functions to ensure transparency, fairness, and compliance with company policies. However, during the audit, it was observed that the committee members were not actively participating in PC related activities.
observations.recommendation: As per policy, functions of PCs are: “General functions of PCs would be as follows: Advise for sourcing strategy. Provide guidance for vendor management. Review and advise on whether proposed procurement actions are in accordance with this Manual. Review that equal opportunity is provided to every genuine competitor. Review and evaluate RFQ, CSQ and related documents submitted. In case of Branches, procurement process shall be handled by BPC. Review negotiated price, terms & conditions, where situation warrants. PC may choose to further negotiate with vendor for pricing, terms and conditions. Review suggestions / complaints by end users and vendors.”
observations.auditee_response: We have noted the concern that committee members were not fully involved in PC proceedings. As our two PC members resigned and we will address this matter to the new members by reinforcing the roles and responsibilities of all PC members and ensuring their proper engagement in all stages of the procurement process.

observations.title: Balance Confirmation Certificates not Provided
observations.description: Branch should provide the balance confirmation certificates for the vendors with whom the business activities are done and staff to whom advances are issued. However, the branch was unable to provide the certain balance confirmation certificates till audit completion date. For detail, please refer to Annexure-D. Further, M/S. “Rang Studio” claimed 60,000 as receivable from the Branch, while as per branch record there is nothing payable to the “Rang Studio”. Work Claimed by the vendor are as below: Sr. No. Description Amount (Rs.) 1 Annual Dinner 35,000 2 Office Frame -Branch Head 10,000 3 Class Group photo Session 15,000
observations.recommendation: For clarity of payables/receivables recorded in books of account, the balance confirmation certificates should be obtained.
observations.auditee_response: It is noted that certain balance confirmations could not be provided by the branch before the completion of the audit. As we asked multiple time from vendor to provide the balance confirmation but most of the vendors ignore this. Regarding the claim by M/s Rang Studio of Rs. 60,000 as receivable, we would like to clarify that, as per our branch record, no amount is payable to Rang Studio and no bill from them is pending at our end. Balance Confirmation from all the sample vendors should be provided within the time limits. Further, the difference of Rs.60,000 with the M/S Rang Studio should be reconciled and books of account should be update at the earliest.

observations.title: Negative Balance of Principal Bank Account
observations.description: As per the company standard practice, balance of bank account should not be negative. During audit it was observed that the ledger maintained for the bank account was revealing credit balance on certain occasions. Such instances are given in table appended below; Sr. No. Date Credit Balance (Rs.) 1 11/07/2025 201,007.83 2 11/07/2025 258,207.83 3 08/03/2022 25,000.00 4 16/08/2023 21,903.40 5 16/08/2023 36,223.40 6 16/08/2023 121,248.40 7 07/09/2022 213,585.02 8 16/08/2023 127,289.40 9 16/08/2023 377,289.40 10 17/08/2023 402,289.40 11 17/08/2023 430,258.40
observations.recommendation: Balance of Principal Bank Account should not be negative.
observations.auditee_response: We have noted the instances where the ledger showed a credit (negative) balance. This was due to wrong BR entry date. Going forward, strict monitoring will be maintained to ensure that the bank ledger always reflects the accurate Debit balance. Recruitment, Payroll & Employees’ Record

observations.title: Incomplete Employees’ Files
observations.description: Employees’ files should be completed in all respects. During checking of files during the audit it was observed that some documents were missing in them as well. Instances are mentioned in Annexure-E.
observations.recommendation: All the employees’ files should be complete and updated. According to policy: “A detailed check list is attached as Annexure-3-P. This check list shall be pasted in the inner side of the file. Branch Head shall ensure that all the required documents are filed in personal files of employees as per the check list pasted in the file”.
observations.auditee_response: It has been noted that certain documents were missing during the audit review. We will thoroughly review all employee files in December, to ensure that the missing documents are collected and properly placed, and implement stricter monitoring to maintain complete and updated records moving forward.

observations.title: Delay in Finalization of Final Settlement Claims
observations.description: As per company policy, final settlement claims should be processed within 45 days from the last working day of an employee. During the current audit, it was noted that final settlement claims of employees were being finalized with significant delay. Details are mentioned in Annexure -F.
observations.recommendation: All concerned authorities should play their role effectively for finalization of final settlement claims within the stipulated time. According to policy: “Final settlement of employees shall be paid within 45 days of their last working days”. Referred to Regional Office
observations.auditee_response: Refer to ROC We are in the process of automating the clearance process, which is expected to significantly reduce turnaround time. However, delays in final settlements—particularly during the period from July to October—primarily occur due to delays in profit calculations at the Corporate Finance end. Additionally, the online issuance of cheques, which can take 2–3 weeks at the signatories’ end, further contributes to these delays. In some cases, delays also arise when employees proceed on uninformed absences, extended leave, or do not rejoin after the completion of their notice period, as end-of-employment settlements are processed based on the last working day. Furthermore, roles such as Librarian and OFA, which require structured and proper handover processes, tend to experience additional delays in the settlement process. Timelines mention in the policies & procedures should be followed by all the Departments, However if the timelines are not practicable, those should be amended through proper procedure.

observations.title: Departure Attendance not marked
observations.description: Attendance should be marked while joining office at the start of day and leaving at day end. During audit, it was observed that some of the employees were not marking departure attendance on regular basis. A few of the instances are mentioned in Annexure G.
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should monitor the attendance record of the branch employees and ensure that the in case of any discrepancy in attendance, staff raise their application for “Attendance Not Marked”, or “Early Leaving” (whichever is applicable) highlighting the reasons. As per policy: “…. Employees shall mark their attendance on biometric devices (online attendance) installed in offices. Further; “Employees are advised to check their attendance on the BEAMS Online Attendance Module regularly to get any errors rectified (e.g. attendance not marked).”
observations.auditee_response: It has been noted that some employees were not marking their departure attendance. We will address this matter by reminding all staff of the mandatory attendance procedure and ensuring stricter compliance going forward.

observations.title: Short Office Hours
observations.description: Branch Head should ensure that complete office hours are being followed by the employees. During sample-based review of employee attendance, it was revealed that some of the branch staff was not following the official timings. The matter may affect operational efficiency of the Branch and also the leave encashment and salary of respective staff. Some of the instances are attached as Annexure-H.
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should monitor the working hours being served by the subordinate staff and in case of nonconformity; necessary steps should be taken for its adaptation. As per policy: “School staff shall report for duty in Branches as per the following: Staff Time In Time Out Teachers on duty 30 minutes before school starts 30 minutes after school ends Admin & Office staff 8 working hours Determined by RO
observations.auditee_response: We will take immediate corrective action by reminding all employees of their official working hours and monitoring compliance more closely.

observations.title: Delay in Confirmation of Employees
observations.description: Employees should be confirmed after completion of probationary period and their confirmation letters issued without any delay. In case, if the branch management needs to extend the probation period, it should be communicated to the concerned employee through probation extension letter. During audit it was observed that confirmation of few employees was issued with delays. Further, no intimation of extension of probation period was made to the concerned employees by the branch management. Annexure-I contains the detail of instances noted during the audit.
observations.recommendation: Probation period should not be un-necessarily prolonged and the office order for the confirmation of services should be issued on timely basis. However, in case of extension in the probation period, office order for such extension should be issued to the concerned employee. As per policy: “Unless otherwise stated in the contract of employment, all employees are required to undergo a probationary period of six (06) working months. In case of unsatisfactory performance, the Line Manager may extend probation period for an additional three (03) months.”
observations.auditee_response: We will review the pending cases immediately and ensure that all confirmations are issued without further delay. Additionally, proper communication regarding any probation extensions will be made to the respective employees going forward.

observations.title: Missing Approval for Blood Relatives & Related Family Members
observations.description: As per policy, blood relatives and related family members shall be hired with the prior approval of Head of HR. It was informed, by branch, that some blood relatives / related family members were working in branch for which approval of HHR was not available. Few of the instances are as under: Sr. # Name ID Name ID Relationship 1 Mr. Sharafat Support Staff Ms. Mehnaz Support Staff Husband/ Wife 2 Mr. Aqeel AMCO Ms. Binish Day Care Husband/ Wife Above stated employees fall under the category as informed by branch.
observations.recommendation: As per policy: “No blood relations and related family members (including but not limiting to husband, wife, parents, children, siblings, grandparents, grandchildren and in-laws) shall be hired in the same Office/Branch; any exception shall be provided by the HHR. However, in no circumstances, one shall be allowed to be in a supervisory capacity of the other or at a position giving rise to a situation resulting in a conflict of interest. If one employee marries another, both may retain their positions provided none is in the same department or supervisory/influential capacity to the other.”
observations.auditee_response: We should ensure strict observance to the policy and will obtain the necessary approval from HR from onwards to avoid future non-compliance.

observations.title: Incomplete Students’ Files
observations.description: All the required documents should be filed in students’ files. Some files were selected and scrutinized during audit and found that the documents e.g. Birth Certificate, Photograph, CNIC of the parents etc. we’re not available in student files. Details are mentioned in Annexure - J.
observations.recommendation: Student files should be complete in all respects. As per policy: “It is the responsibility of the PRO to prepare the file for each student upon finalization of the student admission process. The student file shall remain in the custody of the PRO and may be issued upon request to concerned personnel only e.g. Accounts Office, Teacher and Coordinator etc. A detailed Student File Check List. This checklist shall be pasted on the inside of the file cover. The PRO shall ensure that all the required documents are filed in personal files of students as per the check list pasted in the file.”
observations.auditee_response: Most of the files mentioned in the Audit Report are completed. Whereas the rest will be completed and updated as required.

observations.title: Registration Fee Deposited with Delay
observations.description: As per policy, the registration amount should be deposited on a weekly basis or immediately upon reaching Rs. 10,000. However, as per the detail provided by branch, there were delays in depositing the amount into the bank account. Few of the instances are as follows: Registration ID Receipt Number Amount (Rs.) Date Deposit Slip Date Delay(Excl 7 Days) 367934 5878413 1300 02/09/2021 13/09/2021 4 367952 5878431 1300 02/09/2021 13/09/2021 4 404600 5922383 1400 06/10/2022 19/10/2022 6

observations.title: Overdue Books
observations.description: Books issued, should be returned within stipulated time. It was observed during the audit that some students/teachers did not return the library books. Details are mentioned in Annexure-K.
observations.recommendation: Library books should be returned back according to company’s policy. As per Library Rules in Library Manual Page 21, Clause 10: “Books should not be issued for more than a week”.
observations.auditee_response: The concern is duly noted. The Librarian has been instructed to maintain proper record and follow up with students and teachers for timely return of books.

observations.title: Bar Code Labelling on Library Books not Completed
observations.description: Barcode labelling should be done on library books. During audit we observed that bar code labelling on the library books was not completed Around 600 books were without bar code.
observations.recommendation: The bar code labelling should be completed on timely basis.
observations.auditee_response: Barcode labeling of library books is currently in progress.

observations.title: Books not Accessed in Library Module
observations.description: All library books should be accessed in module. Whereas, contrary to this (according to the librarian) 600 library books were not accessed in the library module KOHA.
observations.recommendation: The entry of Library Books in module should be completed at the earliest.
observations.auditee_response: All these 600 books are outdated and old which will be disposed off.

observations.title: Torn-out Books Found in Branch Library
observations.description: As per the company policy, librarian should check books and get mended/repaired if needed. During audit it was observed that, few library books were with torn out titles/pages which required some repair. Detail of few of such instances is mentioned in Annexure - L.
observations.recommendation: Necessary steps should be taken for repair/ disposal of these books. As per Library Manual Clause 8.1: “To maintain the efficient running of the school library, constant maintaining of resources should be an on-going procedure.  The wear and tear of circulation requires that books should be mended, repaired, bound and re-bound so that they are maintained in a fit condition to be handled”.
observations.auditee_response: The Librarian has been advised to thoroughly check all library books and ensure timely repair or mending or disposed off as per company policy.

observations.title: Low Item Per Child Ratio in Library
observations.description: Item per child should be monitored in school libraries. During audit it was observed that book ratio per child was low in middle section library. As per the item per child report of  June 30, 2025, 4.53 books per student (middle) were available. Whereas the standard book ratio as decided by the Director of Studies is 15 books per child.
observations.recommendation: Keeping in view the students’ strength, the quantity of books should be increased. As per Library Manual clause 18.1; “A school librarian should always be aware of her library material, student strength and items per child”.
observations.auditee_response: Will be purchased books accordingly with budget in this session

observations.title: File for Minutes of Librarian Meeting not Maintained
observations.description: File of minutes of the librarian meeting with regional librarian should be maintained by branch. During the audit it was revealed that branch was not maintaining the file for minutes of the librarian meeting.
observations.recommendation: Librarian should maintain the minutes file for reference as per library manualclause 18.1; “The Regional Librarian should call a meeting once/twice in a academic year of school librarians. All librarians are given minutes of that meeting. The librarian should file these.”
observations.auditee_response: The branch has now started maintaining a dedicated file for the minutes of the librarian meetings with the regional librarian.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Laboratory Stock Registers
observations.description: In order to ensure smooth running of school science laboratories, laboratory stock registers and monthly consumable registers are maintained by laboratory in-charges and checked regularly by BH. Following irregularities were observed: Stock registers were not validated by BH. Stock was not kept systematically, e.g Lab 1 items were kept in Lab 2. Physical stock did not match with records.
observations.recommendation: Laboratory Stock Registers should be checked by BH on monthly basis. As per policy: “Branch Head shall verify the laboratory registers on monthly basis.” Physical balance should be matched with the records.
observations.auditee_response: The Laboratory In-charges have been instructed to update and maintain the stock and monthly consumable registers regularly. The Branch Head will now validate and sign these registers on a monthly basis.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Maintaining Sports Register
observations.description: All stock registers should be maintained properly as per company policies. During the audit, it was observed that Sports Register was not maintained by the branch as per policy. Following are the discrepancies observed: Closing balances were not calculated correctly. Receipts were recorded in issued column. Register was not validated by Branch Head
observations.recommendation: Closing balances should be calculated correctly. Receipts should be recorded in receipt column. Register should be validated by Branch Head
observations.auditee_response: The Sports Stock Register has been reviewed, and the discrepancies highlighted during the audit will be rectify in future.

observations.title: Discrepancies in Maintaining Printed Stationery Register
observations.description: All stock registers should be maintained properly as per company policies. During the audit, it was observed that Printed Stationery Register was not maintained by the branch as per policy. Following are the discrepancies observed: Closing balances were not calculated Correctly. Receipts were recorded in issued column. Register was not validated by Branch Head
observations.recommendation: Closing balances should be calculated correctly. Receipts should be recorded in receipt column. Register should be validated by Branch Head
observations.auditee_response: The Printed Stationery Register has been checked, and the discrepancies highlighted during the audit will be rectify in future.

observations.title: Document Tracking Sheet not in Practice
observations.description: For better control over movement of documents in different offices, document tracking sheet should be attached with the important documents. Contrary to this, the branch was not in practice of attaching the document tracking sheet with the documents being forwarded to different departments.
observations.recommendation: The document tracking sheet should be attached to the documents being forwarded to different departments/offices. As per SOM, Clause, 7.7. DOCUMENT TRACKING SHEET, 1; ““DOCUMENT TRACKING SHEET” attached as Annexure-68 (SOM-025) shall be used on top of every such document(s) which involve movement within different organizational tiers or departments. Main purpose of this sheet is to avoid/identify certain delays during various steps involved to complete document flows. Some of the important ones include:
observations.auditee_response: Noted for the compliance.

observations.title: Purchase Requisition File not Maintained
observations.description: Purchase Requisition file should be maintained for ready reference. It was noted during the audit that Purchase Requisition file was not maintained by the branch.
observations.recommendation: Purchase Requisition file should be separately maintained According to Policy: “There should be following copies of PR. 1st copyRetained by the Branch 2nd Copy For Invoice “
observations.auditee_response: We has now initiated the proper maintenance of the Purchase Requisition file to ensure that all procurement records are readily available for reference.

observations.title: List of Preferred Vendors not Available in the Branch
observations.description: List of Preferred Vendors should be available in the branch. During audit it was observed that the said lists were not available in the branch.
observations.recommendation: List of Preferred Vendors should be available in the branch. As per policy: “For day to day procurement activities, vendors may not be formally registered, but a list of  preferred vendors shall be maintained. Officers responsible for procurement shall prepare a list of  suitable vendors/contractors. This list shall be reviewed/updated by members of the Purchase Committee. The designated Officer will be responsible for maintaining and updating the list.”
observations.auditee_response: We have now ensured that the updated list is properly maintained and readily accessible for reference. It was verified at subsequent audit visit that List of Preferred vendors was started to be maintained by the branch.

observations.title: Track Record of Quotation not Maintained by Branch
observations.description: For procurements valuing more than Rs. 100,000, a track of quotations should be filed separately and made available for verification. It was observed during the audit that track records of such procurements were not kept by the branch.
observations.recommendation: The concerned staff at branch should follow the procedure laid down in policy. According to policy: “For Procurements valuing more than Rs. 100,000 a track of quotations received shall be maintained at Branch duly authenticated by PC to ensure that all quotations received are properly accounted for.”
observations.auditee_response: We have now implemented a proper filing system to ensure that all quotations and related documents for procurements are recorded and readily available for verification.

observations.title: Excess Amount Charged by the Paint Contractor
observations.description: During review, it was identified that paint-work contractor M/s M Shareef Sons claimed excessive measurements in the bills of paint-work executed in the year 2024. The physical measurement was performed by S&A Team in presence of Branch OFA and Branch Assistant Accountant. These measurements were performed in line with the applicability of different paint types i.e. Plastic Emulsion, Enamel, Vinyl Emulsion and Weather Sheet. Branch OFA and Branch Assistant Accountant acknowledged the overcharging of paint area for the year 2024. Summary of excess amount Charged for the year are given as below: Sr. No Paint Area Excess Amount (Rs.) 1 Plastic Emulsion 2,125 2 Enamel 3,567 3 Vinyl Emulsion 11,188 4 Weather Sheet 25,002 Grand Total 41,882
observations.recommendation: Excess amount of Rs.41,882 charged by the Vendor (M/S M Shareef Sons) should be recovered or the amount should be adjusted from the other bills of the vendor.
observations.auditee_response: We cross verified the measurements and tallied them with the bill, identified a difference in the billed amount, contacted the vendor (M. Sharif & Sons) regarding the discrepancy and he agreed to deduct the difference from his payment. The recovery/deduction of Rs. 41,882 need to be made at the earliest from the vendor, with the intimation to relevant personnel of Systems & Audit department.

observations.title: Livery Items Provided with Delays
observations.description: Livery items should be provided to junior staff on time. During audit we observed that livery items were provided to junior staff, with significant delays. Detail of these delays is as under; Session Due Date of Uniform Date of Delivery of Uniform Delay in Months Summer 25 April 2025 28.07.25 3 Winter 24 September 2025 21.01.25 4 Summer 2024 April 2024 20.08.24 3
observations.recommendation: Provision of livery items to Technical and Support staff is necessary for maintaining neatness and uniformity. Livery items should be provided to the junior staff on timely basis. According to the policy: “The procurement procedure shall be initiated within time so as to provide uniform to the staff in April (Summer Uniform) and September (Winter Uniform) or in months suitable to the various Offices/ Branches, determined by RDs for their respective Regions.”
observations.auditee_response: The delay was always from the vendor side due to the workload.

observations.title: Record for Livery Issued not maintained
observations.description: Record for the livery Items issued to Junior staff should be maintained by the branch. It was observed during the audit that Livery Record prior to August 2024 was not available in the branch.
observations.recommendation: Record for the livery items issued to junior staff should be maintained as per policy.
observations.auditee_response: The record was not properly handed over by previous OFA. We will maintain the record in future.

observations.title: Employees Record of Social Security not Available
observations.description: As per Punjab Govt directions, employees having certain salary range (or as prescribed by the notification issued time to time) should be registered with Punjab Employees Social Security Institution (providing hospitalization and dispensary facilities etc.) We observed that PESSI record (including copy of PESSI data form/card) of junior staff was not available and the PESSI Cards were also not issued to the junior staff.
observations.recommendation: Appropriate procedure should be devised and adopted at concerned levels regarding; ➢ Registration of employees. ➢ PESSI record-keeping (for instance PESSI Employee Cards). ➢ PESSI cards issued to the junior staff. Employees should also be informed about the benefits provided by PESSI for example medical care facilities and cash benefits to the secured workers and their dependents.
observations.auditee_response: We will initiate the process of compiling the required records and ensuring the registration of eligible employees in accordance with Punjab Government directives.

observations.title: Sandwich Leaves not Considered
observations.description: As per BSS policies, any gazetted/official leaves that are sandwiched between the employees’ leaves will be accounted for as part of leaves and hence will be charged to the employee. During scrutiny of attendance record we found that in few instances the sandwich leaves were not accounted for. Details are mentioned below: Employee ID Employee Name Leave Before Off Day Leave Type Off Day(s) Leave After Off Day Leave Type 16808 Muhammad Riaz 01/07/2022 Sick Leave 02/07/2022 - 03/07/2022 04/07/2022 Annual Leave 16808 Muhammad Riaz 07/05/2021 Sick Leave 08/05/2021 - 16/05/2021 17/05/2021 Sick Leave 40013 Naveed Alam 05/07/2024 Annual Leave 06/07/2024 - 07/07/2024 08/07/2024 Annual Leave 40291 Muhammad Fayyaz 08/11/2024 Casual Leave 09/11/2024 - 10/11/2024 11/11/2024 Sick Leave 92922 Muhammad Ismail 03/01/2025 Sick Leave 04/01/2025 - 05/01/2025 06/01/2025 Annual Leave 92922 Muhammad Ismail 15/06/2024 Sick Leave 16/06/2024 - 19/06/2024 20/06/2024 Casual Leave
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should ensure compliance to the company policies. The branch accountant should keep a keen eye on these while preparations of salary. As per policy: “Off days or gazetted holidays falling in between leave periods (sandwiched) shall be counted as part of that leave. For example, if leave is applied for on a Friday and Monday, then Saturday and Sunday will be included in the leave”.
observations.auditee_response: These leave are auto adjusted by Beams. The leaves which are not auto dealt by the system, those should be reported to RO-HR to account for as per policy.

observations.title: Employees not Registered in EOBI
observations.description: The process for registration in EOBI should be started immediately after hiring of an employee. However, it was observed during audit that certain employees were not registered in EOBI. Detail of these employees is given in Annexure-M.
observations.recommendation: EOBI registration should be immediately made and updated in module, after the joining of the employee.
observations.auditee_response: All employees are registered in EOBI only there EOBI no. are not updated on Beams will updated soon. It was verified at subsequent visit that all EOBI numbers were updated in BEAMS.

observations.title: Unconfirmed Employees in the Branch
observations.description: Employees should be confirmed after completion of probationary period and their confirmation letters should be issued without any delay. In case, if the extension of probation period is necessary, it should be communicated to the concerned employee through probation extension letter. During audit we found that confirmation of certain employees was not made, till the time of our audit. Detail of these employees is given in Annexure-N.
observations.recommendation: Probation period should not be un-necessarily prolonged and the office order for the confirmation of services should be issued on timely basis. However, in case of extension in the probation period, office order for such extension should be issued to the concerned employee.
observations.auditee_response: Two employees resigned and one is confirmed now.

observations.title: Registration Fee Deposited prior to the Collection
observations.description: As per Company Policy Registration fee collected should be deposited on weekly basis. It was observed during the audit that in BEAMS certain registration fee collections were deposited prior to their collection dates. Apparently, the deposit dates were wrongly fed by the concerned person. Instances are mentioned as Annexure-O.
observations.recommendation: Branch Head should ensure that all the receipts and deposited are correctly fed in the system.
observations.auditee_response: Mistakenly deposit date was wrongly entered.

observations.title: Discrepancies in the List of Canteen’s Assets
observations.description: List of canteen owner’s assets should be prepared and duly signed by the Contractors and the Branch Head. During the audit, it was observed that the detail of canteen contractor’s assets was not signed and verified by the contractor and the Branch Head .
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that the detail of Canteen Owner’s assets, duly signed and validated by both parties of the contract, should be kept in the branch to differentiate the assets of Company and assets of Contractor.
observations.auditee_response: It will be complete as per your recommendation.

observations.title: Discrepancies in the List of Photocopier’s Assets
observations.description: List of Photocopier’s assets should be prepared and duly signed by the Contractor and the Branch Head. During the audit, it was observed that the detail of Photocopier’s assets was not verified by the Branch Head. Further the list was not updated since year 2023.
observations.recommendation: It is recommended that the detail of latest Photocopier’s assets, duly signed and validated by both parties of the contract, should be kept in the branch to differentiate the assets of company and assets of Contractors.
observations.auditee_response: It will be complete as per your recommendation.

observations.title: Un-Numbered Assets
observations.description: All the Fixed Assets should be numbered against which it is issued. During current audit, some un-numbered assets were observed in the branch. Instances are given in Annexure-P.
observations.recommendation: All the Fixed Assets should be numbered as per Fixed Asset Register. As per policy: “Fixed Assets’ codes shall be affixed to them by the Caretaker/Accountant, on timely basis, in accordance with the Company’s policy.”
observations.auditee_response: Most of the un numbered assets are related to Furniture and Fixtures, whose numbers were removed due to repainting and frequent cleaning. However, we will re-affix the numbers as per the recommendation.

observations.title: Un-Traced Assets
observations.description: As per the company policy, it is the responsibility of School Heads to ensure the safe custody of fixed assets. But while physical checking of fixed assets, some fixed assets appearing in the fixed assets’ register, were not physically present in the branch. Instances are given in Annexure-Q.
observations.recommendation: Missed fixed assets should be traced by the branch. According to policy: “It shall be the primary responsibility of BH to ensure safe custody of the assets of the Company”.
observations.auditee_response: In this case, almost all school assets have been counted. If any asset # became unreadable during cleaning, it may have been marked as untraced. All such items are available in the branch. Due to time limitation and nature of untraced items, it is recommended to recheck all untraced items during yearly stock take activity of the branch.

observations.title: Un-Matched Assets Found in the Branch
observations.description: During current audit some assets were observed as un-matched i.e. the fixed assets that were present in the branch but not appearing in fixed assets’ register of the branch. Detail is attached as Annexure-R.
observations.recommendation: The source from which these assets were received should be identified and fixed assets’ register should be updated after consulting the matter with RO.
observations.auditee_response: We will recheck all these numbers with the current FAR and rectify accordingly.

observations.title: Duplicate Numbers of Assets
observations.description: All the Fixed Assets should be numbered with the Codes assigned to them. During physical verification of assets, some double-numbered assets were observed in the Branch. Detail of instances are mentioned in Annexure-S.
observations.recommendation: All the Fixed Assets should be numbered as per Fixed Asset Register. As per Policy: “Upon receipt of codes, Designated Officer of User Office shall affix these codes on respective fixed assets immediately. Such codes shall be affixed in a systematic and permanent manner”.
observations.auditee_response: We will recheck all these numbers with the current FAR and rectify them accordingly.

observations.title: Out of Order Assets Found in Branch
observations.description: All assets should be kept with due care; any damaged asset should be repaired or disposed-off. During physical verification many assets were found for which repair work/disposal was not initiated by the branch. Detail is attached in Annexure-T.
observations.recommendation: Out of order assets should be disposed-off if they are not repairable. According to the Policy: “Assets are sold when: Assets are beyond repair or where the cost of repair is considerably high and it is considered appropriate to buy a new asset. Assets are obsolete The Company, for any other reason, has no use for the assets”.
observations.auditee_response: We are aware of the out-of-order assets in the branch. We will evaluate each item, and if repairable, it will be fixed subject to budget availability. The remaining assets will be processed for AIDN as per your recommendations.

observations.title: Assets Disposed Off but Still Available in FAR
observations.description: Assets against which AIDN is processed should be removed from the FAR and the assets should also be handed over to the vendor. It was observed during the audit that there were certain assets which were disposed off against formal AIDN but they were still appearing in FAR. Detail is attached in Annexure-U.
observations.recommendation: Asset disposed off should be removed from Branch’s FAR and the assets should not be physically present in the branch.

observations.title: Assets Disposed Off but still Present Branch

It was observed during the audit that there were certain assets which were disposed off against AIDN but they were physically available in the branch. Detail of such assets are mentioned in the Annexure-V.
observations.recommendation: Asset disposed off should not be physically available in the branch.
observations.auditee_response: During the review, duplicate numbering was observed on these assets. The records will be corrected as per the updated FAR.

observations.title: Assets Never used since Purchase

It was observed that certain assets provided to branch were not used since purchase. Detail of such assets are mentioned in the Annexure-W.

observations.title: Demolition Register not Prepared

observations.recommendation: Demolition register should be maintained by branch for scrap. Its utilisation/disposal shall be recorded in the same register.”
observations.auditee_response: Register will be maintained as per recommendation. Science laboratory

observations.title: Actual Consumption not Recorded in Laboratory Stock Registers
observations.description: In order to ensure accurate record keeping of science laboratories, actual consumption of the laboratory items should be recorded in the stock registers. It was observed during the audit that rather than recording the actual consumption, stocktake was carried out on certain intervals and the difference was posted in the consumption.
observations.recommendation: Consumption should be recorded on actual basis.
observations.auditee_response: The branch will initiate accordingly.

observations.title: Ex-Armed Forces Personnel not provided by Security Company
observations.description: The armed guards at the branch are provided by Zims Security Services Private Limited. It was observed during scrutiny of the security guards’ that none of the 6 armed guards of the school were having ex-armed forces background, while Security Company has to provide 50% ex-armed forces personnel.
observations.recommendation: Armed guards should be provided to the branch in accordance with the contract- As per the contract, “Security Company has to provide 50% ex-armed forces personnel”. It is therefore recommended that the non-compliance of security services contract be reported to concerned office and followed up on until issues are resolved.
observations.auditee_response: Noted for compliance.

observations.title: Assembly area Unmarked
observations.description: Emergency exits and Assembly areas should be clearly marked ensuring smooth evacuation of buildings. It was observed that “assembly area” were labelled in branch. Further the allocation of designated assembly area for specific group of students were not marked such as Primary Section, Middle Section, Senior Section, etc.
observations.recommendation: Assembly area should be clearly labelled as per the emergency plan of branch in order to ensure smooth evacuation.
observations.auditee_response: Necessary steps will be taken in future.

observations.title: No Scanning Room at Gate No. 3
observations.description: During the audit, it was observed that there was no scanning room available at Gate No. 3 of the branch, while a number of visitors, parents and students entered in the branch from the same. However, walkthrough gate was installed at the gate and was operational too.
observations.recommendation: Scanning Room should be available at each entry for visitors.

observations.description: Security control room is one of the most important area in any branch. Since security equipments and centralized systems such as CCTV backups, Public Address System, Hooters and alarms etc are installed and operated from security room, therefore, it should be situated in a well secured place with highly restricted access. observations.title: Expenditure Exceeded the Budgeted Amount
observations.description: Budgetary limits for each expense head should be kept in view while making spending. The review of system generated “Budget Variance Sheets” shows that significant overspending was made under the following heads: Computer Repair & Maintenance (2022-23) Building Repair & Maintenance (2022-23) Direct Cost – Air Conditioner Repair (2022-23 & 2024-25) Bank Charges (2022-23, 2023-24 & 2024-25) Detail of significant unfavorable variances (account head wise), for financial year 2022-23, 2023-24 and 2024-25 is attached as Annexure-L.
observations.recommendation: Overspending in a particular account head may result in shortage of funds allocated for other account heads or may create need for additional budget. Significant overspending should be controlled/monitored by the Branch Head. Efforts should be made to spend budgeted amounts in accordance with their allocation. According to “Audit & Financial Control, 4. Bank, Cash & Payment Process, 3. Branch Operational Budget (Imprest)”, Clause # 5 of INDEX; “Budget variance shall be monitored for judicious use of funds allocated under all Heads of Expenses. System generated budget variance sheet be consulted to monitor variance of expense against budget allocation and discrepancy, if any, rectified.”
observations.auditee_response: Computer Repair & Maintenance (2022-23) , Building Repair & Maintenance (2022-23) , Direct Cost – Air Conditioner Repair (2022-23) overspending in these heads occurred prior to our joining. In the future, we will make our best efforts to avoid overspending in any head.  Direct Cost – Air Conditioner Repair (2024-25) In this head we save in 451 Branch Rs 99,947/- but due to new building expense we book in 443.  Bank Charges (2022-23, 2023-24 & 2024-25) No budget is made under this head, but expenses are mandatory under this head such as new cheque book charges and etc.
